Embabel Agent Framework
Embabel (Em-BAY-bel) is a framework for authoring agentic flows on the JVM that seamlessly mix LLM-prompted interactions
with code and domain models. Supports
intelligent path finding towards goals. Written in Kotlin
but offers a natural usage
model from Java.
From the creator of Spring.
Key Concepts
Models agentic flows in terms of:
Actions
: Steps an agent takes
Goals
: What an agent is trying to achieve
Conditions
: Conditions to assess before executing an action or determining that a goal has been achieved.
Conditions are reassessed after each action is executed.
Domain model
: Objects underpinning the flow and informing Actions, Goals and Conditions.
Plan
: A sequence of actions to achieve a goal. Plans are dynamically formulated by the system, not the programmer.
The
system replans after the completion of each action, allowing it to adapt to new information as well as observe the
effects of the previous action.
This is effectively an
OODA loop
.
Application developers don't usually have to deal with these concepts directly,
as most conditions result from data flow defined in code, allowing the system to infer
pre and post conditions.
These concepts underpin these differentiators versus other agent frameworks:
Sophisticated planning.
Goes beyond a finite state machine or sequential execution
with nesting by introducing a true planning step, using a
non-LLM AI algorithm. This enables the system to perform tasks it wasn’t programmed to do by combining known
steps in
a novel order, as well as make decisions about parallelization and other runtime behavior.
Superior extensibility and reuse
: Because of dynamic planning, adding more domain objects, actions, goals and
conditions
can extend the capability of the system,
without editing FSM definitions
or existing code.
Strong typing and the benefits of object orientation
: Actions, goals and conditions are informed by a domain
model, which can
include behavior. Everything is strongly typed and prompts and
manually authored code interact cleanly. No more magic maps. Enjoy full refactoring support.
Other benefits:
Platform abstraction
: Clean separation between programming model and platform internals allows running locally
while
potentially offering higher QoS in production without changing application code.
Designed for LLM mixing
: It is easy to build applications that mix LLMs, ensuring the most cost-effective yet
capable solution.
This enables the system to leverage the strengths of different models for different tasks. In particular, it
facilitates
the use of local models for point tasks. This can be important for cost and privacy.
Built on Spring and the JVM,
making it easy to access existing enterprise functionality and capabilities.
For example:
Spring can inject and manage agents, including using Spring AOP to decorate functions.
Robust persistence and transaction management solutions are available.
Designed for testability
from the ground up. Both unit testing and agent end to end testing are easy.
Flows can be authored in one of two ways:
An annotation-based model similar to Spring MVC, with types annotated with the Spring stereotype
@Agent
, using
@Goal
,
@Condition
and
@Action
methods.
Idiomatic Kotlin DSL with
agent {
and
action {
blocks.
Either way, flows are backed by a domain model of objects that can have rich behavior.
We are working toward allowing natural language actions and goals to be deployed.
The planning step is pluggable.
The default planning approach is
Goal Oriented Action Planning
.
GOAP is a popular AI planning algorithm used in gaming. It allows for dynamic decision-making and action selection based
on the current state of the world and the goals of the agent.
Goals, actions and plans are independent of GOAP. Future planning options include:
Plans created by a reasoning model

data.title: Show HN: Spegel, a Terminal Browser That Uses LLMs to Rewrite Webpages
data.author: simedw
data.article_summary: Spegel是一款概念验证的终端浏览器，通过大型语言模型（LLM）处理网页HTML，并以Markdown格式在终端显示。用户可根据自定义提示调整网页内容，满足个性化需求，如简化文章或提取关键步骤。Spegel从网页获取HTML内容，通过配置文件中的提示进行处理，并使用Textual将结果渲染为Markdown。它不支持POST请求，主要用于探索和个性化内容展示，而非替代传统终端浏览器。用户可以通过pip安装Spegel，并配置自己的提示和视图以获得不同浏览体验。项目源代码可在GitHub上查看和贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用LLM（大型语言模型）重构网页内容的不同技术方案及其潜在应用

不同观点：
• **优化网页浏览体验**：[__MatrixMan__] 提出一种想法，希望网页能够智能判断是否需要在每次访问时重写页面，从而避免重复处理。这将提高浏览效率，尤其对于内容较为固定的网页。

• **对LLM内容反刍的担忧**：[nartho] 对LLM重复输出内容表示不满，并提到Browsh项目，该项目采用与LLM无关的技术在终端渲染HTML，提供了一种不同的网页浏览方式。

• **LLM对表情符号的偏好**：[WD-42] 提出一个轻松的问题，好奇为什么LLMs在输出中偏爱使用表情符号，但未深入讨论技术细节。

• **LLM过滤内容的潜力**：[mromanuk] 认为LLM可以有效过滤SEO优化带来的冗余信息，提取出核心内容，如在食谱网站中去除不必要的部分。

44433409.article_content:
Spegel - A Terminal Browser That Uses LLMs to Rewrite Webpages
June 23, 2025
TL;DR Spegel is a proof-of-concept terminal web browser that feeds HTML through an LLM and renders the result as markdown directly in your terminal.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Two weekends ago, after my family had gone to sleep, I found myself unsupervised with a laptop and an itch to build something interesting. A couple of hours later, I had a minimal web browser running in my terminal (no JavaScript, GET requests only) that transformed web content based on my custom prompts.
Then, a few days later, Google released Gemini 2.5 Pro Lite, significantly faster inference speed, suddenly my little weekend hack became a tad more practical.
Personalisation
Adapting content to suit individual needs isn’t a new idea, think about translating books or summarising lengthy articles. However, this used to be slow and expensive. LLMs have changed this dramatically, making these transformations quick and easy.
Spegel ("mirror" in Swedish) lets you explore web content through personalized views using your own prompts. A single page can have multiple views, maybe one simplifying everything down to ELI5 or another highlighting key actions. It's entirely up to you and your prompting skills.
Sometimes you don't want to read through someone's life story just to get to a recipe.
That said,
this is a great recipe
Example configuration
[[views]]
id
=
"recipe"
name
=
"Recipe"
hotkey
=
"7"
order
=
"7"
enabled
=
true
auto_load
=
false
description
=
"Get to the point in recipes"
icon
=
"🍳"
prompt
=
"""Parse a recipe and extract only the essential parts.
Format the output like this:
# Ingredients
* 1 tbsp salt
* 400 g beef
# Steps
1. Preheat the oven to 200°C (Gas Mark 6).
2. Wash and chop the carrots.
-----
**Instructions:**
* Use **metric units** (not imperial).
* inches -> cm
* pounds -> kg
* cups -> dl
* Keep the output **clean and minimal** no extra commentary, tips, or nutrition facts.
* Include the servings."""
How it works
The pipeline is straightforward.
Spegel fetches HTML content, processes it through an LLM using prompts stored in a config file (~/.spegel.toml), and outputs markdown rendered via Textual. Prompts and views can be adjusted live during a browsing session.
This was my first experience using Textual for a TUI, and it's been delightful, possibly too delightful, as I found myself adding a few unnecessary interface elements just because it was easy.
One gotcha was ensuring only completed lines (ending in newline characters) were streamed; otherwise, the markdown renderer would parse incomplete markdown and fail to recover formatting

Other terminal browsers
There are a lot of great terminal browsers out there, Lynx and Links2 are close to my heart. There are also modern attempts like Browsh that can even render graphs using half-block Unicode characters (▄█).
Spegel isn’t meant to replace these, it’s more of an exploration or proof-of-concept. It currently doesn't support POST requests (though I have some ideas on handling
<form>
elements by creating on-the-fly UIs).
But most modern websites aren’t designed with terminal browsing in mind. They rely on CSS and JS, making them cumbersome in small terminal windows, full of clutter and noise. Spegel tries to clear away distractions, providing content tailored more closely to your needs.
Try it
Spegel is still in the early stages, so expect some rough edges, but it’s usable and kind of fun to play with.

data.article_summary: ORNL研究人员通过在碳纤维复合材料中加入聚丙烯腈（PAN）纳米纤维层，成功将其抗拉强度提升了一倍。碳纤维常用于航空航天和高性能车辆，但其与聚合物基体的界面结合较弱。研究团队利用超级计算机模拟了500万个原子，发现直径约6纳米的PAN纳米纤维能有效增强材料强度，通过电纺技术制备这些纳米纤维并应用于界面，可改善应力分布，提升复合材料整体强度。该研究发表在《Advanced Functional Materials》期刊上，有望推动航空、车辆制造等领域使用更强、更轻的材料。

Simulations reveal the secret to strengthening carbon fiber
June 19, 2025
ORNL researchers found a way to double the tensile strength of carbon-fiber composites by reinforcing the material with a thin layer of PAN nanofibers. A human hair is approximately 100 times wider than one of these fibers. Credit: Carlos Jones/ORNL, U.S. Dept. of Energy
Stronger than steel and lighter than aluminum, carbon fiber is a staple in aerospace and high-performance vehicles — and now, scientists at the Department of Energy’s Oak Ridge National Laboratory have found a way to make it even stronger.
ORNL researchers simulated 5 million atoms to study a
novel process for making carbon-fiber composites stronger and more cost efficient
by incorporating a reinforced layer of polyacrylonitrile nanofibers, or PAN nanofibers. Led by ORNL’s Carbon and Composites group, the team combined fundamental science with molecular dynamics simulations using the Frontier supercomputer to better understand how the reinforcement process works at the atomic scale. Their findings,
published in the journal
Advanced Functional Materials
, could lead to new, ultradurable materials for airplanes, vehicles and a wide range of manufacturing applications that require stronger, more lightweight materials.
Carbon-fiber composites are made by embedding thin strands of carbon — each thinner than a human hair — into a polymer matrix. Carbon fiber strands are incredibly strong; however, their bond with the surrounding polymer is somewhat weak by comparison.
“When a carbon-fiber composite fails, it typically begins at the interface between the carbon-fiber strands and the polymer matrix,” said Tanvir Sohail, a postdoctoral researcher at ORNL’s National Center for Computational Sciences. “By incorporating a layer of PAN nanofibers at the interface, we redirect stress from the carbon fibers into the surrounding polymer, which improves load distribution and enhances the composite’s overall strength.”
The process of reinforcing the carbon-fiber composites involves a technique called electrospinning, which uses an electric field and a spinning drum to create a spool of PAN nanofibers no larger than 10 nanometers. For comparison, a single sheet of paper is about 100,000 nanometers thick.
Carbon fiber is expensive to manufacture and test, and running extensive physical experiments can quickly become time consuming and cost prohibitive. That’s where supercomputing can drastically accelerate the search for materials with the desired characteristics and help guide the experimental development. But simulating the synthesis process is also expensive — computationally, that is.
“Carbon fiber is extremely dense, and modeling it with molecular dynamics requires tracking the behavior of millions, if not billions, of atoms,” said ORNL computational scientist Swarnava Ghosh, who led the Frontier simulations along with Sohail.
The material is assembled and tested for strength. Strands of PAN fibers with varying diameters are bundled and tightly bonded to a polymer coating for reinforcement. A graphene sheet is used to simulate pulling on the material to identify weak points. Credit: ORNL, U.S. Dept. of Energy
Most high-performance computing clusters used by industry and universities can simulate upwards of a few thousand atoms. But the calculations use approximation techniques that group atoms together instead of calculating them individually. The technique is faster and far less computationally demanding, but it’s also less accurate and can introduce errors.
The research team was given a small allocation of time on Frontier via a Director’s Discretionary award to demonstrate the benefits of using a leadership-class supercomputer. Frontier is the world’s most powerful supercomputer for open science, with a peak performance of 2-exaflops per second, meaning it can perform more than a billion-billion calculations per second.
Using only a fraction of Frontier’s power, Sohail and Ghosh built a 5-million-atom model of carbon-fiber composites reinforced by PAN nanofibers. This model provided unprecedented molecular-level insights into the fundamental forces that bind the materials together.
To find the right fit, the team modeled PAN nanofibers with diameters that ranged between 6 and 10 nanometers by using the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator, or LAMMPS. LAMMPS is a powerful, open-source code used for molecular dynamics simulations on supercomputers. It is widely used to model the behavior of atoms in materials such as metals, polymers and biomolecules and investigate how the materials respond to conditions such as stress, temperature and chemical changes over time.

44399838.article_summary: ORNL研究人员通过在碳纤维复合材料中加入聚丙烯腈（PAN）纳米纤维层，成功将其抗拉强度提升了一倍。碳纤维常用于航空航天和高性能车辆，但其与聚合物基体的界面结合较弱。研究团队利用超级计算机模拟了500万个原子，发现直径约6纳米的PAN纳米纤维能有效增强材料强度，通过电纺技术制备这些纳米纤维并应用于界面，可改善应力分布，提升复合材料整体强度。该研究发表在《Advanced Functional Materials》期刊上，有望推动航空、车辆制造等领域使用更强、更轻的材料。
44399838.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：碳纤维材料在乐器制造中的应用及其相关问题

  - [lucas_membrane] 认为碳纤维由于其耐用性和一致性，是高质量乐器批量生产的理想材料，尤其在热带硬木乐器价格高涨的背景下。文章中提到的让碳纤维变得更薄、更轻、更强的技术改进，可能对乐器市场有重大影响。

  - [iamleppert] 分享了个人经验，认为碳纤维类似于石棉，对健康有潜在危害。他提到在使用碳纤维PLA打印时，通过显微镜观察到皮肤中嵌入了微小的碳纤维，且这些纤维可能漂浮在空气中，对健康造成威胁。

data.title: RP2350pc Open Source Hardware all in one computer
data.author: AlexeyBrin
data.article_summary: RP2350pc是一款开源硬件电脑，搭载RP2350B双核ARM/RISC-V处理器，内置520KB RAM、8MB PSRAM和16MB闪存。它具备四个USB端口、两个UEXT连接器、DVI/HDMI输出、音频编解码器、麦克风输入、耳机输出、音频放大器、SD卡槽和LiPo电池支持，通过USB-C供电和编程，配有电源开关。该设备适合用于构建类似复古的ARM/RISC-V电脑，支持键盘和电视，可用于游戏和教育。目前，Veselin Sladkov正在开发支持Apple ][、Oric Atmos和Puldin 601模拟的Reload模拟器，而Paul Robson则在开发统一API，以便创建编译器和操作系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于基于RP2350的小型单板计算机（SBC）及其外围设备和功能的讨论

不同观点：
• nfriedly提到该SBC类似于Adafruit的Fruit Jam，也是基于RP2350构建的，并提供了产品链接。
• Retr0id对RP2350如何通过D+/-引脚实现USB主机功能表示困惑，因为根据其理解，RP2350只能通过PIO实现该功能。
• raphlinus对该项目表示赞赏，并提到其已订购。他还提到pico-dvi-rs项目具有早期原型，并指出其在字体处理上的独特性，鼓励使用Rust语言进行开发。
• kevin42认为在小型处理器上集成过多外设会导致内存占用问题，尽管它是一个很好的原型平台。

补充讨论：
• Lerc建议可以通过使用2或4个RP2350来增强板子的功能，而成本不会显著增加。他还提到可以通过开源方式自行研究和实现。
• chaosprint对选择ES8311单声道音频编解码器表示不解，并提到自己正在使用AIC3204进行项目开发，认为其是更好的选择。
• rasz进一步指出ES8311是低功耗单声道音频编解码器，而使用立体声编解码器如TLV320AIC320x成本也仅略高，猜测可能是为了符合“中国制造2025”政策以获取补贴。

争议焦点：
• 对于音频编解码器的选择存在争议，chaosprint和rasz都对使用ES8311单声道音频编解码器表示不解，并提出其他可能的替代方案。

data.title: Aesop in Words of One Syllable
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 《Aesop in Words of One Syllable》是一本独特的儿童读物，出版于19世纪，属于玛丽·戈多芬（Mary Godolphin）创作的“单音节”系列。该书用简单的单音节词汇重写了伊索寓言，旨在让孩子们更容易阅读。玛丽·戈多芬本名露西·艾金（Lucy Aikin），是英国著名的历史学家、诗人和女性主义者，对儿童教育有浓厚兴趣。这本书包含99个寓言故事，如《狼来了》和《狐狸与葡萄》，但像《龟兔赛跑》等故事因无法用单音节词表达而未收录。该书通过Distributed Proofreaders和Project Gutenberg等志愿者项目得以保存和传播。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对使用单音节词重述经典作品的看法及相关讨论

不同观点：
• [pinko] 认为作者在使用单音节词的限制时作弊，比如使用连字符将双音节词“butchers”分割开，以符合规则。
• [gweinberg] 指出坚持使用单音节词有点愚蠢，因为人们最早学习的词往往是双音节的，比如重复的音节。
• [teraflop] 猜测这种做法可能启发了Guy Steele的“Growing a Language”演讲，或者他们独立得出了相似的想法。
• [esafak] 支持这种做法，但指出维多利亚时代的英语翻译对于孩子来说过于复杂，需要简化后孩子才能理解，并举例说明了翻译的复杂性。
• [cckolon] 联想到Randall Monroe对简单英语的执着，通过链接提供了一个相关的xkcd漫画。
• [josefritzishere] 提供了背景信息，指出这种使用单音节词的书籍在1900年左右由Henry Altemus Company出版，且有一整个系列。
• [JKCalhoun] 更喜欢在Archive.org而不是Project Gutenberg上查看参考书，并个人不喜欢在每个故事结尾标明道德。
• [vintermann] 认为这种做法更像是一种游戏，而不是有效的教学工具，指出即使偶尔使用多音节词也不会对孩子造成困难，且认为作者在游戏中“作弊”。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了对单音节词限制是否有效的争议，特别是对儿童读物的适用性。
• 有人提到这种做法可能受到其他作品或演讲的启发，提供了一个文化背景的参考。
• 对具体书籍和翻译的讨论，特别是维多利亚时代语言风格的复杂性，提供了实际例子来说明观点。
• 不同读者对道德教育和语言简化的个人偏好也有所体现。

44433843.article_content:
Hot off the Press
Book Reviews and News from Distributed Proofreaders
Home
About
Aesop in Words of One Syllable
In the 19th Century, British and American children’s literature evolved from puritanical moral and religious instruction to delightfully imaginative tales meant to awaken a sense of wonder. But morality and imagination could certainly thrive together.
Æsop’s Fables in Words of One Syllable
is an excellent example of this.
The ancient Greek storyteller
Aesop
may or may not have existed, and he may or may not have written the hundreds of morality tales attributed to him. Yet his stories have been popular from the time of Aristotle to the present day, and their morals have contributed classic expressions like “sour grapes” to the English language. The first English version, printed by William Caxton in 1484, was intended for adults. In the 16th and 17th Centuries, English schoolboys were taught Latin and English from various translations of the fables. It wasn’t until the 18th Century that the fables began to appear in illustrated editions intended to entertain (while edifying) children. And in the 19th Century, with the flowering of children’s literature, there was a veritable explosion of illustrated Aesops.
Æsop’s Fables in Words of One Syllable
is unique among the illustrated editions: It’s written entirely in words of one syllable (except for the title, of course). It’s part of a “One Syllable” series written between 1867 and 1870 by Mary Godolphin, the pen name of
Lucy Aikin
. Aikin was a prominent English historian, poet, and feminist who also took a keen interest in the education of children. Other books in her “One Syllable” series include
Robinson Crusoe
,
The Swiss Family Robinson
, and
The Pilgrim’s Progress
. They’re all designed to make reading them easy for children.
The Aesop volume, in an 1895 edition published after Aikin’s death, contains 99 fables, including those featuring the boy who cried wolf, the fox and the grapes, and the goose that laid the golden (“gold”) egg. Notably absent are “The Tortoise and the Hare” and “The Ant and the Grasshopper,” perhaps because Aikin couldn’t come up with one-syllable synonyms for some of those creatures. But there’s plenty here to enjoy, thanks to the volunteers at Distributed Proofreaders and Project Gutenberg.
This post was contributed by Linda Cantoni, a Distributed Proofreaders volunteer.

data.title: First-Class Models: The Missing Productivity Revolution
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对复杂工具的接受度、工具的灵活性与复杂性之间的平衡、版本控制与数据模型的应用

不同观点：
• jdvh认为，工具的复杂性增加会大幅减少其潜在用户群。他以Git和Hypercard为例，说明大多数人只会使用他们熟悉的工具，复杂的版本控制和分支管理会让用户感到困惑和失去兴趣。
• GiorgioG指出，业务环境是动态的，而软件数据模型相对僵化。Excel因其灵活性受到欢迎，用户可以快速构建和调整模型以解决当前问题。
• taeric认为，对于许多假设性问题，追求“权威数据”和“不变性操作”可能会成为障碍。用户需要能够自由编辑和探索不同参数，即使这意味着允许不完整或不良状态的存在。
• carterschonwald同意问题的存在，但建议将交易和对立方的授权作为解决方案的核心，强调需要更具互动性和增量性的系统设计。

不同观点：
• [tastyfreeze] 认为使用硅胶猫砂可以成功制作钠硅酸盐，并计划下次尝试使用破碎玻璃。这表明他正在探索不同材料在化学实验中的应用，且对使用常见材料（如猫砂和玻璃）进行实验持开放态度。
   
• [busssard] 关注的是地质聚合物的回收问题，对如何有效回收新制备的地质聚合物提出疑问。这显示出他对材料的可持续性和环保性有更高的关注，而不仅仅是如何制作这些材料。

补充讨论：
• [tastyfreeze] 通过实际实验验证了使用猫砂制作钠硅酸盐的可行性，并计划进一步实验（如使用破碎玻璃），表明其对材料科学实验具有实践兴趣。

• [busssard] 的问题揭示了关于地质聚合物生命周期的一个重要问题，即这些材料在使用后的处理和回收问题，这可能引发对可持续材料开发的更深入讨论。

争议焦点：
• 材料的获取和使用是否可持续：[tastyfreeze] 关注如何从常见材料中制作钠硅酸盐，而 [busssard] 则质疑这些新材料的回收和环保性，提出了材料生命周期管理的问题。

• 实验材料的可行性与环保性的平衡：两种观点反映了对材料选择的两种不同优先级——一种关注实验的可行性与材料的可得性，另一种则关注实验材料在整个生命周期中的环境影响。

data.title: I am not a supplier (2022)
data.author: wofo
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了软件供应链的概念及其问题。作者指出，过去几年中，关于软件供应链的讨论增多，尤其在LeftPad事件后以及一系列安全事件发生以来。软件供应链指的是项目中所使用的各种依赖库及其管理，这些库通常通过开源软件（FOSS）许可证自由使用和重新混合，避免了法律和财务麻烦。现代软件项目可能包含数百甚至数千个依赖项。

供应链概念源于制造业，指生产过程中所需的各级供应商。在软件中，类似问题如库的所有者停止提供访问或引入安全漏洞，可能影响整个互联网。软件供应链的管理工具如软件物料清单（SBOM）用于记录项目使用的库及其信息。

作者认为，将FOSS纳入传统供应链定义是误导的，因为开源库的维护者与商业供应商不同，他们不承担商业供应链中的责任和关系管理。文章呼吁对开源库的维护和安全进行更好的管理，以避免“远程操控”风险。

44434355.article_content:
I am not a supplier
31 Dec 2022 - Thomas Depierre
For the past few years, we have seen a lot of discussions around the concept of the Software Supply Chain. These discussions started around the time of LeftPad and escalated with multiple incidents in the past few years. The problem of all the work in this domain is that it forgets a fundamental point.
Before we get there, I am going to define what is usually meant by Supply Chain and suppliers, why we are applying to software. And then why attempts at bringing FOSS under that definition are deeply misguided.
The concept
In the past couple of decade, we have seen the rise of Free and Open Source Software (FOSS). In particular, this has enabled a massive growth of the reuse of pieces of codes, packaged as libraries. This has been possible due to a massive ecosystem of infrastructure that bloomed around that idea. Package Managers exist for every programming language environment under the sun nowadays, with central repositories holding the metadata needed to find the libraries and handle their distributions.
This has been possible due to the FOSS Licenses being pretty lenient, enabling a reuse and remix of these libraries without the massive legal and financial headache that would come otherwise. A modern software project will probably have hundreds if not thousands of these dependencies, from OpenSSL to a test framework or a datepicker, across a wide spectrum covering things like a JSON encoder/decoder library or even the libc of the OS it is deployed on.
This ecosystem of dependencies, a lot of them transitive (dependencies of a dependency), is what the Software Supply Chain model calls the Supply Chain of the project. Inside this model we will find tools that help manage it, like a Software Bill Of Materials (SBOM) that is supposed to hold the information of what libraries are used for this project, where they were found, which version, some hash of the content, etc.
What is a Supply Chain
The idea of a Supply Chain does not come out of nowhere of course. In the manufacturing industry, the supply chain is the long chain of suppliers needed to produce a particular factory’s output. As an example, if you assemble cars, you need seats, a lot of screws, cables, electronics, all kinds of stamped metal sheets, … Your cable supplier needs copper, plastic, energy and probably all kinds of machine tools. Machine tools that probably need other machine tools to be built, screws, bolts, nuts, some electronics too… And we can keep going through this long game of “what do you need to produce this car” until your diagram looks like a massive spaghetti ball.
And then someone in an unknown small factory in Germany gets sick and it happens that five levels higher in the chain everyone depends on their particular bolt, and we are all screwed. A version of this problem happened early in the work to deliver the vaccine for the Covid19, when supply chain specialists realised they would need a lot more glass vials than could be produced in a year worldwide.
In order to avoid this kind of snag five levels deep in the chain that would end up stopping their valuable production, manufacturing companies have spent a lot of effort over the years to build relationships with their suppliers, at every level of the process. It is both a really deep relationship and usually never enough, but isn’t that the case of every complex system?
Why do we talk of Software Supply Chain today ?
Well because companies keep discovering that they have big problems in their products, and that it does not come from the code their software engineers wrote. The problem can come from the owner of a library deciding to stop providing access to it (Leftpad for example) and breaking half the Internet.
Or it could come from a massive library used for mundane digital infrastructure (Like OpenSSL or Log4J) discovering they have massive security problems that make half the Internet easy to pwn.
Or someone could talk to the people owning these libraries, convince them they are here to help, get access and add a crypto mining code to it for their own profit (so many cases that I do not know where to start).
Or the owner of the code could decide that he does not like people supporting a warmongering regime, so he will add code that destroys the computer of the engineers using his code, if they live in this part of the world (yes there have been a few instances of this too).
And then, everyone in these companies discover that their product is open to spooky “action at a distance” from code they did not know about. So the concept of “Software Supply Chain” comes in, to define all the things that need to be done by the people in the supply chain, the owners of these libraries, in order to be good citizens that do not break companies using the code downstream.
These rules govern things like how we test the code, how we protect who has access to it, how we release versions, how we validate its safety, how we organise work on

data.title: Pbf2sqlite: Reading OpenStreetMap into a SQLite Database
data.author: amadeuspagel
data.article_summary:
**pbf2sqlite** 是一个命令行工具，用于将 OpenStreetMap 的 .osm.pbf 文件读取到 SQLite 数据库中。主要功能包括：

- 读取 .osm 或 .osm.pbf 文件到指定数据库。
- 可选择添加 R*Tree 索引、地址表和图形表。
- 示例命令：`pbf2sqlite test.db read country.osm.pbf`，将 `country.osm.pbf` 文件数据读取到 `test.db` 数据库中。

该工具使用 GPL-3.0 许可证，主要用 C、Python、Shell 和 Makefile 编写。OSM 数据可从如 Geofabrik 等供应商获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SQLite是否具备类似PostGIS的地理信息系统（GIS）能力，或者仅仅是通过传统数据库基本类型存储数据。

不同观点：
• **SQLite不具备原生的GIS能力**：一些评论者指出，SQLite本身不像PostgreSQL有PostGIS那样的原生GIS扩展。SQLite主要依赖于传统的数据库类型（如文本、数字、二进制数据）来存储空间数据。这意味着在处理复杂的地理空间查询时，SQLite可能不如PostGIS那样功能全面。

• **通过SpatiaLite扩展提供GIS功能**：另一观点提到，虽然SQLite没有内置的GIS功能，但可以通过SpatiaLite扩展来实现类似的功能。SpatiaLite是SQLite的一个模块，提供了与PostGIS类似的地理空间数据类型和函数。因此，通过使用SpatiaLite，SQLite也可以执行空间查询、几何操作等GIS任务。

• **SQLite与PostGIS的性能和功能对比**：有评论者提到，即使通过SpatiaLite扩展，SQLite在处理大型地理空间数据集和高并发访问时的性能可能不如PostGIS。PostGIS是专门为PostgreSQL设计的地理空间扩展，具有更多优化和功能，适用于复杂的GIS应用场景。

补充讨论：
• **使用场景的考虑**：一些评论者指出，选择使用SQLite的SpatiaLite还是PostGIS，应该根据具体的使用场景来决定。如果应用需要轻量级、嵌入式的地理空间数据处理，SQLite可能是一个不错的选择；而对于需要高性能、高并发和复杂空间分析的应用，PostGIS则更为合适。

• **开发和维护成本**：有观点认为，使用SpatiaLite可能会增加开发和维护的复杂性，因为需要额外安装和配置扩展模块，而PostGIS作为一个成熟且广泛使用的解决方案，可能在生态系统和社区支持上更为丰富。

总结：SQLite本身不具备原生的GIS能力，但可以通过SpatiaLite扩展来实现类似功能。然而，与PostGIS相比，SQLite在处理复杂和大规模地理空间数据时可能存在性能和功能上的不足，选择使用哪种方案应根据具体需求和场景来决定。

- 读取 .osm 或 .osm.pbf 文件到指定数据库。
- 可选择添加 R*Tree 索引、地址表和图形表。
- 示例命令：`pbf2sqlite test.db read country.osm.pbf`，将 `country.osm.pbf` 文件数据读取到 `test.db` 数据库中。

该工具使用 GPL-3.0 许可证，主要用 C、Python、Shell 和 Makefile 编写。OSM 数据可从如 Geofabrik 等供应商获取。

主要讨论点：SQLite是否具备类似PostGIS的地理信息系统（GIS）能力，或者仅仅是通过传统数据库基本类型存储数据。

不同观点：
• **SQLite不具备原生的GIS能力**：一些评论者指出，SQLite本身不像PostgreSQL有PostGIS那样的原生GIS扩展。SQLite主要依赖于传统的数据库类型（如文本、数字、二进制数据）来存储空间数据。这意味着在处理复杂的地理空间查询时，SQLite可能不如PostGIS那样功能全面。

• **通过SpatiaLite扩展提供GIS功能**：另一观点提到，虽然SQLite没有内置的GIS功能，但可以通过SpatiaLite扩展来实现类似的功能。SpatiaLite是SQLite的一个模块，提供了与PostGIS类似的地理空间数据类型和函数。因此，通过使用SpatiaLite，SQLite也可以执行空间查询、几何操作等GIS任务。

• **SQLite与PostGIS的性能和功能对比**：有评论者提到，即使通过SpatiaLite扩展，SQLite在处理大型地理空间数据集和高并发访问时的性能可能不如PostGIS。PostGIS是专门为PostgreSQL设计的地理空间扩展，具有更多优化和功能，适用于复杂的GIS应用场景。

补充讨论：
• **使用场景的考虑**：一些评论者指出，选择使用SQLite的SpatiaLite还是PostGIS，应该根据具体的使用场景来决定。如果应用需要轻量级、嵌入式的地理空间数据处理，SQLite可能是一个不错的选择；而对于需要高性能、高并发和复杂空间分析的应用，PostGIS则更为合适。

• **开发和维护成本**：有观点认为，使用SpatiaLite可能会增加开发和维护的复杂性，因为需要额外安装和配置扩展模块，而PostGIS作为一个成熟且广泛使用的解决方案，可能在生态系统和社区支持上更为丰富。

总结：SQLite本身不具备原生的GIS能力，但可以通过SpatiaLite扩展来实现类似功能。然而，与PostGIS相比，SQLite在处理复杂和大规模地理空间数据时可能存在性能和功能上的不足，选择使用哪种方案应根据具体需求和场景来决定。

data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Sci-Hub创始人Alexandra Elbakyan通过发行名为$SCIHUB的memecoin来为平台筹集资金的实验。Sci-Hub自2011年创建以来，提供了数百万篇通常需付费获取的学术论文，成为学术界的重要资源。然而，Elbakyan因侵犯版权面临法律诉讼，包括2015年Elsevier在美国法院胜诉并获赔1500万美元。由于传统资金来源受限，她转向加密货币，于2024年11月推出$SCIHUB token，目标为Sci-Hub筹集运营资金。尽管初期市值达到2000万美元，并通过token liquidation筹得50万美元，但实验并不顺利，memecoin未如预期增长。Elbakyan的政治和学术观点独特，常与主流学术界和出版商产生冲突，这使她成为学术自由运动中的标志性人物。文章还探讨了学术出版的经济问题和加密货币筹资的潜力与挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术论文的访问与出版模式的变革

不同观点：
• **支持Sci-hub的开放访问模式**：tastyfreeze认为，Sci-hub实现了研究论文的自由获取，这种模式应当推广，因为限制访问前沿研究成果只会阻碍科学进展和个人自学。Sci-hub的开放获取方式应成为未来学术出版的标准，只有出版商自身会对此感到不满。

• **Sci-hub的局限性**：虽然Sci-hub解决了访问问题，但tastyfreeze指出，它仅满足了部分需求。要取代传统学术期刊，还需要在出版、审稿和发现（论文检索）等功能上有所突破，这些方面并不容易实现。

• **去中心化出版系统的设想**：tastyfreeze提出，未来可能通过一个去中心化的、联合的系统实现学术出版的变革。在这个系统中，论文作者可以自行运行服务器发布和托管论文，并能够订阅其他作者的服务器。这种模式将避免再次陷入“付费发表、付费阅读”的陷阱。

补充讨论：
• **传统期刊的附加价值**：tastyfreeze提到，学术期刊除了提供论文访问外，还涉及出版、审稿和发现等功能。这些功能在当前的学术生态中仍然具有重要价值，也是Sci-hub模式尚未涵盖的部分。

• **对印刷期刊的需求**：尽管大多数学术需求可以通过数字化方式满足，但tastyfreeze也指出，部分大学可能仍然需要印刷版的期刊，不过这一需求可以通过现有的按需印刷技术轻松满足。

争议焦点：
• **Sci-hub的合法性与道德问题**：尽管Sci-hub为大众提供了免费访问学术论文的途径，但其行为在法律和道德层面存在争议。出版商认为其侵犯了版权，而支持者则认为知识应当自由传播。

• **去中心化系统的可行性**：tastyfreeze设想的去中心化出版系统虽然在理论上能够解决当前系统的弊端，但其实际操作和维持的可行性仍待验证，特别是在学术界广泛采用和维持质量控制方面。

Alexandra Elbakyan in Sochi 2021
By Alexandra Elbakyan - Own work, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=111943946
Alexandra Elbakyan
has been called many things: "Science's Pirate Queen," a "Robin Hood of science," and by Nobel laureate Randy Schekman, simply "a hero." The 36-year-old Kazakhstani computer programmer created Sci-Hub in 2011, a website that provides free access to millions of academic papers normally locked behind expensive paywalls. According to a 2018 study, Sci-Hub provides access to nearly all scholarly literature.
Now, Elbakyan is experimenting with perhaps the most unlikely funding mechanism yet:
memecoins
.
In November 2024, anonymous supporters launched
$SCIHUB
, a community-driven cryptocurrency token designed to fund Sci-Hub's operations. The project reached a $20 million market cap and raised $500,000 from a 2% token liquidation by Elbakyan, with 20% of the total token supply dedicated to Sci-Hub funding. But the unconventional funding experiment has been anything but smooth.
The Academic Publishing Controversy
To understand why Elbakyan has turned to cryptocurrency, one must first grasp the economics of academic publishing. Researchers produce knowledge in the form of research papers that do not belong to them, while a few mighty businesses make huge amounts of money from it. Publishers like Elsevier charge universities thousands of dollars for journal subscriptions, creating what
critics call a "double-dipping
" system where institutions pay both to produce research and to access it.
While working on her brain-computer interfaces diploma project, Elbakyan discovered the paywall problem with accessing journal articles, as her university did not have access to many publications related to her work. Her solution was characteristically direct: she created a PHP script that bypassed publisher paywalls to download papers for free.
MORE FOR YOU
The impact was immediate and massive. Sci-Hub contains 88 million research papers and serves 80+ million users annually. But it also made Elbakyan a target. In 2015, Dutch publisher Elsevier sued Sci-Hub in U.S. court, winning a $15 million judgment and forcing Elbakyan into hiding due to the risk of extradition.
The case echoes the tragic story of
Aaron Swartz
, the internet activist who was prosecuted for downloading millions of academic articles from JSTOR in 2011. Facing decades in prison, Swartz died by suicide in 2013.
Ars Technica
has compared Elbakyan to Swartz, and his death cast a long shadow over debates about academic access and prosecutorial overreach.
Alexandra Elbakayan: The Eccentric Revolutionary
Elbakyan herself cuts an unusual figure in the world of academic activism. Born in Almaty, Kazakhstan, she identifies as multiracial, with Armenian, Slavic and Asian roots, and was raised by a single mother who was an accomplished computer programmer. She started programming at age 12 and performed her first computer hack at 14, using SQL injection to obtain access to all logins and passwords of her home internet provider.
Her political views are equally unconventional. Elbakyan has stated that she is inspired by communist ideals and considers the common ownership of ideas to be essential for scientific progress. She views the current system of producing knowledge in science as "a classical example of a failed capitalist system" where "researchers are being exploited."
These views have sometimes put her at odds with mainstream academia. According to her interview, she was attacked on the Internet by 'science popularizers' who supported liberal views that led to the shutdown of Sci-Hub in Russia in 2017 for a few days. In December 2019, The Washington Post reported that Elbakyan was under investigation by the US Justice Department for suspected ties to Russia's military intelligence arm, the GRU, allegations she has denied.
Enter the Memecoin
Given these controversies, traditional funding sources have remained largely closed to Sci-Hub. The platform has relied primarily on Bitcoin donations, but these have been inconsistent. Sci-Hub paused database updates for years, potentially due to funding constraints.
This funding crisis led to the $SCIHUB token experiment. The project combines viral meme coin appeal with meaningful cause, featuring active recipient support from Elbakyan (featured on Sci-Hub homepage) and transparent blockchain structure.
But the project has been plagued by complications that highlight both the promise and perils of cryptocurrency funding.
In a lengthy Twitter post in June 2025, Elbakyan revealed problems with the original token:

data.title: Writing Code Was Never the Bottleneck
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了软件工程中的真正瓶颈并非编写代码，而是代码审查、知识传递、测试、调试以及协调和沟通的人力成本。尽管LLM（如AI工具）加快了代码生成速度，但它们并未减少理解、测试和信任代码所需的努力。生成的代码可能引入不熟悉的模式或破坏既有惯例，增加了审查和维护的复杂性。LLM加快了初始实现，但并未解决根本问题——代码理解仍是难点，团队仍需依赖信任和共享的上下文。软件工程本质上是协作的，LLM无法替代清晰的思考、仔细的审查和周到的设计。因此，编写代码的成本虽降低，但团队共同理解代码的成本并未改变，这仍是主要瓶颈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的难点和挑战

不同观点：
• [kevin42] 认为软件开发中的难点并不在于写代码本身，而在于将业务需求转化为技术设计和实现。他指出，在瀑布模型中这一问题尚可解决，但需求往往在最终用户看到产品之前并不明确，因此敏捷开发显得尤为重要。他还提到，凭借30多年的软件开发经验，写代码从来不是成功交付项目的难点。

• [ajd555] 完全同意[kevin42]的观点，并进一步补充了自己在软件开发中遇到的实际困难，包括与非技术项目经理的沟通、处理自视甚高的“明星”开发者、维护遗留代码、预见设计缺陷或观察盲点，以及处理生产环境中的棘手bug和召集合适人员解决问题。他强调，软件开发中最难的部分往往是与人相关的部分，而不是技术本身。

• [devstein] 对[kevin42]和[ajd555]的观点表示完全赞同，并提到自己因此创办了Dosu（https://dosu.dev/），旨在重新思考软件工程中的“知识”方面。

补充讨论：
• [ajd555] 强调了人类经验和非正式合作在解决问题中的重要性，例如通过私人关系请运维人员帮忙解决问题，而不是依赖于花费大量资金或使用代币。

• 争议焦点：在软件开发中，写代码是否是项目的难点。这三位评论者一致认为，写代码并不是最难的部分，真正的挑战在于需求转化、与人沟通和处理遗留问题等。

Writing Code Was Never The Bottleneck
Post
🔗
Writing Code Was Never The Bottleneck
Published
June 30, 2025
I'm on X at
@ordepdev
.
For years, I’ve felt that writing lines of code
was never
the bottleneck in software engineering.
The actual bottlenecks were, and still are,
code reviews
,
knowledge transfer
through mentoring and pairing,
testing
,
debugging
, and the human overhead of
coordination and communication
. All of this wrapped inside the labyrinth of tickets, planning meetings, and agile rituals.
These processes, meant to drive quality, often slow us down more than the act of writing code itself because they require thought, shared understanding, and sound judgment.
Now, with LLMs making it easy to generate working code faster than ever, a new narrative has emerged: that writing code
was
the bottleneck, and we’ve finally cracked it.
But that’s
not quite right
.
The marginal cost of adding new software is approaching
zero
, especially with LLMs. But what is the price of
understanding
,
testing
, and
trusting
that code?
Higher than ever
.
LLMs shift the workload — they don’t remove it
Tools like Claude can speed up initial implementation. Still, the result is often more code flowing through systems and more pressure on the people responsible for reviewing, integrating, and maintaining it.
This becomes especially clear when:
It’s unclear whether the author fully understands what they submitted.
The generated code introduces unfamiliar patterns or breaks established conventions.
Edge cases and unintended side effects aren’t obvious.
We end up in a situation where code is more straightforward to produce but more complex to verify, which doesn’t necessarily make teams move faster overall.
It’s not a new challenge. Developers have long joked about
“copy-paste engineering”
, but the velocity and scale that LLMs enable have
amplified those copy-paste habits
.
Understanding code is still the hard part
“The biggest cost of code is understanding it — not writing it.”
LLMs reduce the time it takes to produce code, but they haven’t changed the amount of effort required to reason about behavior, identify subtle bugs, or ensure long-term maintainability. That work can be even more challenging when reviewers struggle to distinguish between generated and handwritten code or understand why a particular solution was chosen.
Teams still rely on trust and shared context
Software engineering has always been collaborative. It depends on
shared understanding
,
alignment
, and
mentoring
. However, when code is generated faster than it can be discussed or reviewed, teams risk falling into a mode where
quality is assumed rather than ensured
. That creates stress on reviewers and mentors, potentially slowing things down in more subtle ways.
LLMs are powerful — but they don’t fix the fundamentals
There’s real value in faster prototyping, scaffolding, and automation. But LLMs don’t remove the need for
clear thinking
,
careful review
, and
thoughtful design
. If anything, those become even more important as more code gets generated.
Yes, the cost of writing code has indeed dropped. But the cost of making sense of it together as a team
hasn’t
.
That’s still the bottleneck. Let’s not pretend it isn’t.

data.title: phkmalloc
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者如何改进FreeBSD中的内存分配函数malloc，以解决内存分页和释放时性能低下的问题。最初的malloc实现（来自Chris Kingsley）在虚拟内存环境下表现不佳，尤其在程序终止时会出现明显的磁盘活动（称为"死亡嘎嘎声"现象）。作者通过记录内存分配和释放的日志，发现问题在于释放内存时需要遍历空闲块列表，导致未使用的内存也被调入RAM。作者通过在空闲块前添加结构体，避免直接操作未使用内存，显著减少了死亡嘎嘎声现象。最终，作者彻底重写了malloc实现，并通过数据收集和绘图分析进一步优化了性能。

补充讨论：

• 评论还暗示了历史上曾有过类似的彻底 redesign，nasretdinov可能在隐含地比较当前技术变革的规模与历史上导致系统重构的技术变革。
• 核心争议焦点在于，当前的系统设计是否已经足够灵活，能够应对硬件的多核化和NUMA架构的挑战，还是说需要像过去一样进行一次彻底的重新设计。

phkmalloc
phkmalloc
¶
Jason Evans laid
jemalloc
to rest yesterday, and gave a kind shoutout to my malloc, aka.
“phkmalloc”, and it occured to me, that I should write that story down.
I wrote a little bit about it in my article for the
30 year aniversary issue of the FreeBSD Journal
but there is more to it than that.
Why
¶
In FreeBSD we inherited Chris Kingsley’s malloc implementation from
BSD, it worked, and we had much larger fish to fry, so we paid it
no attention.
During 1994 and 1995, RAM prices went through the roof, and therefore,
conciously or subconciously, efficient use of RAM became a concern.
In my case it became a huge concern, because my machine only had
4MB RAM and being release engineer, I ran GCC a lot.
My system paged more than I thought it should, and in particular
I noticed a very distinct burst of disk-activity whenever GCC
terminated.
The “death-rattle” was even more prominent with Tcl and Tk programs.
That made no sense to me, why would things page when the program
was freeing things prior to termination ?
The “canonical” malloc implementation, the malloc implementation to
start all malloc implementations, is in chapter 8.7 in The C
Programming Language, and as all code in that book it is simple and
elegant:  A linked list holds the free blocks of memory, and that
is pretty much it.
If you are up for a challenge:  Go read chapter 8.7 now, and see if
you can predict what comes next :-)
The problem
¶
K&R’s malloc was written on a swapping system, probably a PDP-11,
where either the entire process is in memory or the process does
not run.
In the meantime we had gotten Virtual Memory, where pages may or
may not be in RAM when you need them, but the kernel handles that,
so from a programmes point of view, the only difference is that
sometimes a memory access causes disk activity.
Chris Kingsley’s malloc starts with this comment:
/*
* malloc.c (Caltech) 2/21/82
* Chris Kingsley, kingsley@cit-20.
*
* This is a very fast storage allocator.  It allocates blocks of a small
* number of different sizes, and keeps free lists of each size.  Blocks that
* don't exactly fit are passed up to the next larger size.  In this
* implementation, the available sizes are 2^n-4 (or 2^n-10) bytes long.
* This is designed for use in a virtual memory environment.
*/
So clearly he had thought about the swap/paging thing, and yet,
performance felt less than stellar and there was that death-rattle
phenomena.
The first things I did was to hack a version of the malloc, to log
all calls to malloc(3), free(3) and realloc(3) to a file and tried
to make sense of the, for the time, vast amount of data that produced.
It was pretty obvious from my PostScript plots, that performance
was far from stellar, and even more obvious that the death-rattle
was associated with freeing a lot of memory.
Why would
freeing
memory cause the kernel to page things in and
out ?
To
free(3)
a block of memory, you have to walk the free-list to
find the right place to insert it, and the linked list is stored
in the first couple of words of all the free chunks.
Worst case, to free a chunk of memory, we have to read the first
couple of words of all the memory not currently use.  The death-rattle
was the kernel paging all the memory the process explicitly did not
use, into RAM, so the process could mark even more memory as
explicitly not used.
I may have exclaimed “Duh!” at this point.
The fix(es)
¶
I went to work fixing this, and my first hack was brutal:  Whenever
a chunk was to be freed, I would chop a small struct from front of
the first free chunk on the free list:
struct free_chunk {
struct free_chunk       *next;
struct free_chunk       *prev;
void                    *chunk;
size_t                  length;
};
And put that structure on the free list, so that I would never have
to touch the actual free memory again, unless it was reallocated.
That nearly eliminated the death-rattle, and things ran markedly faster.
Calling
free(3)
with only a pointer, and no size, means malloc
implementations need some “trick” to remember how big that chunk
was when it was allocated.
K&R malloc, and every other malloc, hides that in a small struct
right before the chunks:
free(ap)  /* put block ap in free list */
char *ap:
{
register HEADER *p, *q;
p = (HEADER *)ap -1;  /* point to header */
[…]
That bugged me, because it meant that a chunk of memory which had
been unused for a long time (in VM-traffic terms) before the process
calls
free(3)
still get paged into RAM just to mark it unused.
That reminded me of a trick I had seen on a very old and very strange
computer, which needed to keep track of stuff on the drum memory.
Biting the bullet
¶
So I blew away all of Chris’ code and started from scratch.
Along the way I collected a lot of data and plotted it on
my inkjet printer, and one of those plots still have a
place in my heart and on my wall, I call it “Towers of
Barad-dûr”:
I will not

data.title: Jane Austen's Boldest Novel Is Also Her Least Understood
data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对简·奥斯丁小说《曼斯菲尔德庄园》的理解和评价

不同观点：
• [gwd的观点]  
   1. 《曼斯菲尔德庄园》的结局虽然看似圆满，但其实是偶然的结果。亨利·克劳福德的决定性行为（如没有回去检查管家）引发了一系列事件，导致故事的最终走向。  
   2. 奥斯丁对当时流行的许多小说的缺陷感到不满，她的作品往往通过细微和颠覆性的方式对当时的小说进行回应和批判。

• [ggm-at-algebras的观点]  
   1. 《曼斯菲尔德庄园》是他自20世纪80年代以来的最爱，但大多数奥斯丁粉丝似乎不喜欢这部作品，认为主角软弱无味。  
   2. 他不同意这种看法，认为主角体现的是一种内向、胆怯的性格，并且在家庭中受到欺负。  
   3. 小说中涉及到的加勒比财富实际上与奴隶制有关，虽然主角埃德蒙没有明确表现出对家族财富来源的担忧，但这是值得注意的历史背景。  
   4. 他还提到，在海军晋升中，性交易是常见的，这反映了当时社会现实的一个侧面。

补充讨论：
• [tosser0001的观点]  
   1. 提到惠特·斯蒂尔曼的电影《大都会》中，角色们曾辩论《曼斯菲尔德庄园》的价值，暗示该小说在不同观众中有争议性。

争议的焦点：
• 《曼斯菲尔德庄园》的主角性格及其意义：[gwd]认为故事的结局是偶然的，而[ggm-at-algebras]则强调主角的内向和被欺负的性格，并从社会历史角度解读小说。  
• 小说中涉及的历史背景，如奴隶制和海军晋升中的性交易，是否应该被更深入地理解和讨论。

data.title: Gridfinity: The modular, open-source grid storage system
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: Gridfinity Generator是由Perplexing Labs推出的一款在线工具，允许用户自定义设计网格存储系统的bins、底板、盖子等，只需输入尺寸即可。Gridfinity是一个模块化存储解决方案，尺寸以42x42x7毫米为基准，具有高效、组织性和安全性，免费开源且几乎全部可通过3D打印制作。该系统由Alexander Chappels设计，灵感部分来源于Zack Freedman的初始设计，现已成为一个社区项目，任何人都可使用和修改。目前该网站仍在开发中，欢迎加入Discord社区参与改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gridfinity存储系统的不同观点和实际应用

不同观点：
• **支持DIY和废物利用**：
  - [jot] 和 [tetha] 提到可以使用厕所卷筒或废旧纸板作为Gridfinity的墙壁，减少材料浪费和打印时间。
  - [tetha] 认为与其花费大量时间打印Gridfinity组件，不如直接用废旧纸板制作存储解决方案。

• **支持使用现成解决方案**：
  - [WillAdams] 经历了从购买塑料收纳盒到转向DIY解决方案的过程，以避免等待运输和产品下架的问题。
  - [morjom] 提到了其他类似的开源或模块化存储系统，如Honeycomb storage wall和Cargo modular storage system，提供更多选择。

• **对网格大小和空间浪费的争议**：
  - [Gigachad] 指出Gridfinity的抽屉大小不总是网格大小的整数倍，导致空间浪费问题，并提到使用非标准网格可以解决但会失去兼容性。
  
• **定制化和批量生产的讨论**：
  - [stevenpetryk] 认为Gridfinity项目如果能够批量生产会更好，这样用户可以把时间花在打印更定制化的组件上。
  - [SparkyMcUnicorn] 提到使用OpenSCAD进行定制，比如添加磁铁等功能，以满足特定需求。

• **对项目实用性的怀疑**：
  - [nancyminusone] 对Gridfinity项目的实际用途表示怀疑，认为这可能只是工具组织爱好者的兴趣，并且会增加塑料使用量。
  - [kalev] 和 [PeterStuer] 提到初次接触Gridfinity时对其用途感到困惑，认为增加一些图片或说明会有帮助。

补充讨论：
• **工具的CAD模型获取**：
  - [SOLAR_FIELDS] 提出如何将实际工具快速转化为CAD模型的问题，寻求DIY领域可行的解决方案。

• **推荐视频和频道**：
  - [slau] 和 [wnolens] 推荐了Zach Freedman的视频频道和使用卡纸板制作存储的视频，认为这些资源对项目有帮助。

争议焦点：Gridfinity系统在实际应用中的空间利用效率和定制化需求之间的平衡。

44421776.article_content:
Hi there,
Look!
The new version of
Ensō
(codename: Occult Vampire Keanu) is available for public testing!
Download it here
This is a temporary icon I used for testing. I am considering creating a simplified version of it. PS. here's the
original image
(on
potato.horse
, of course)
What's included
Following
MISS
, my focus is on removing distractions over adding new features. This can be surprisingly challenging (e.g. how do I tell users about feature X or Y without breaking their flow?) but also gives me time to focus on polishing the app.
(we will discuss these in more detail in future posts)
Short version (as explained by Hermes Trismegistus)
Simplified, more accessible UI
Accessible themes
Coffeeshop Mode
Privacy improvements
Slightly longer version:
An even more simple, streamlined UI, following the
MISS
philosophy.
Most of the UI has been moved to the application menu bar for easier discoverability and shortcut access. So far no one has missed the old inline UI, but you can read more about it towards the end of this note.
5½ Accessibility-friendly themes to choose from
We have
6
5½ predefined themes focussed on accessibility and specific use patterns based on feedback I've collected over the years.
writing during the day in regular light conditions
writing in bright light
writing in low light
writing in low light for devices with OLED screens
allows for perfect black
writing in extremely low light conditions, with reduced light exposure  (See
Midnight
,
Obsidian for Vampires
)
designed for OLED screens
the main use case here is writing at night, to put myself to sleep.
5½ and not 6 because one theme still needs some work. Is there a specific use case or theme you'd like to see in Ensō? Let me know!
Coffeeshop Mode™
This is one of the few truly new features in Ensō. Coffeeshop mode allows you to stop worrying that someone standing behind you might see what you're typing. The text itself is concealed but you still know what you're writing.  Use
⌘-C
to toggle on and off at any time.
I've been using it for a couple of months and found it super helpful, especially for journaling in public places, but not only (read more here:
Sketch - Ensō Coffeeshop Mode
).
A few smaller accessibility improvements
Note: if you remove the
Edit
menu and call it
Write
, MacOs won't add its AI crap to your settings.
toggle autocorrect, autocapitalise, spelling
control text size (previously not possible in the native version)
A new, polished text rendering engine
The new text rendering engine allows for better control over typography settings, supports alternative display modes like Coffeeshop, and uses a custom caret.
I don't know how to describe it objectively (and I obviously lack the distance to) but writing in the new UI feels different, more fluid. The text is easy to read, but also somewhat softer (though not blurry).
Less is more, so why do I care about it?
Because
less is more. I want Ensō to feel familiar and high-quality, like a good Moleskine notebook. I want people to feel comfortable paying $10 for a typing app without text selection. I want them to enjoy it as much as I do. Fewer features allow me to focus more on what
is
there.
AppStore by default (but standalone versions are still coming)
Ensō will be published via the AppStore by default. We will keep the old version on Gumroad, but there's no reason to maintain it, since the new version is better in every possible way and functionally the same by default.
The reasons I decided to
skip the AppStore and use Gumroad
, plus what I learned from that are beyond the scope of this note (you can click the link to request that particular write-up).
Why?
several users complained that Gumroad payment looked, for the lack of a better word, shady, especially at the step with a PayPal payment screen. The ones who messaged me still bought the app, but I imagine there were many who turned back.
AppStore with all its flaws makes delivering apps... slow and annoying, but also relatively easy without much code.
I can add OTA updates and re-publish Ensō via Gumroad later, which makes sense as an iterative improvement.
The Gumroad version of Ensō will stay as a backup, but will not be maintained.
What's not included
Analytics
I've been using Ensō daily for 6 years. I've also received a ton of high-quality feedback, not via analytics but from users who were kind enough to reach out to me. I like to think that I have a fairly good idea of how and why people use Ensō.
The previous version of Ensō would pass an anonymous impression event on load. Now, by design, no network traffic is made at all. Here's our new Privacy Page.
Current version of our Privacy page (
source
)
Related
How I Use Analytics With My Indie Projects
and
Defaults Matter, Don't Assume Consent
Personalisation
It will come, but the new version is already so much better than the previous, that I feel like waiting for more features would be a wasted opportunity.

data.author: pamoroso

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Interlisp网站、模拟器以及Lisp机器的现状与未来

不同观点：
• phaer：认为Interlisp的网站提供了丰富的信息，并提供了一个在线模拟器，方便用户访问和体验Interlisp。提供了具体链接，强调其实用性和资源丰富性。

• kps：个人虽然没有深入使用过Interlisp，但拥有相关硬件（Xerox Daybreak）的实际操作经验，并提到曾参与与Interlisp相关的项目（在DEC Alpha上运行的模拟器）。他还提到对NetBSD的Ultrix兼容性做出了一些贡献，展示了历史项目与现代系统的联系。

• jshaqaw：对Interlisp团队的工作表示赞赏，但提出一个不同的观点，认为当前更需要的是“未来的Lisp机器”，而不是单纯的重现过去的技术。强调创新和未来发展的必要性。

• pfdietz：引用了一段关于Interlisp-D的描述，强调该系统规模庞大，包含大量代码行数（Lisp代码17,000行，Bcpl代码6,000行，微代码4,000行）。通过具体数据展示了Interlisp的复杂性和开发难度，表达了对这一庞大系统的欣赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：jshaqaw认为当前应关注Lisp机器的未来创新，而不仅仅是复古重现。这与其他参与者对Interlisp历史和重现的关注形成对比，反映了不同用户对技术发展方向的不同期待。

• 历史与现代的联系：kps的经验展示了Interlisp在历史项目中的应用，以及如何与现代系统（如NetBSD）产生联系，提供了技术演进的视角。

• 技术复杂性：pfdietz通过具体数据展示了Interlisp系统的复杂性，为讨论增加了技术深度的维度。

整体来看，讨论围绕Interlisp的技术重现、历史应用、未来发展以及技术复杂性展开，参与者提供了各自的见解和经验。

不同观点：

• terminalbraid针对具体科学细节进行纠正，指出文章中关于铍同位素（8Be）的描述有误，强调普通的铍核是9Be，并解释了8Be由于半衰期极短且不属于束缚态，不能算作常规的原子核。

• 争议的焦点之一是科学理论的评价和态度问题。libraryofbabel对现代科学理论持负面看法，而chasil则关注具体科学概念如无中子核聚变，二者态度形成对比。

• terminalbraid针对具体科学细节进行纠正，指出文章中关于铍同位素（8Be）的描述有误，强调普通的铍核是9Be，并解释了8Be由于半衰期极短且不属于束缚态，不能算作常规的原子核。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是科学理论的评价和态度问题。libraryofbabel对现代科学理论持负面看法，而chasil则关注具体科学概念如无中子核聚变，二者态度形成对比。

• terminalbraid的评论集中在科学准确性上，对具体科学描述中的错误进行指正，并提供了相关的维基百科链接以支持其论点。

• 科学理论的有效性和科学家的坚持是另一个潜在的讨论点，libraryofbabel的观点暗示了对科学界在某些领域坚持未成功理论的不满。

data.title: Converting a large mathematical software package written in C++ to C++20 modules
data.author: vblanco
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了将大型数学软件包从C++转换为使用C++20模块系统的经验。传统上，C++软件包通过头文件定义接口，这种方式效率低下。C++20引入了模块系统，通过导出和导入机制提高编译效率。作者以一个包含约80万行代码的有限元库为例，描述了一种同时支持头文件和模块接口的转换方法，讨论了遇到的挑战和实际效果。结果显示，虽然转换需要一定努力，但能有效减少库本身的编译时间，而下游项目的编译时间变化不明显。文章最后探讨了未来几十年内整个数学软件生态系统转换到模块系统的长期策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：模块化对编译时间和代码结构的影响，以及与其他优化方法（如预编译头文件、LLMs应用）的比较

不同观点：
• npalli认为，模块化在减少编译时间（约10%）和改善代码结构方面有明显的好处，但对下游项目的编译时间影响不明确。他还提到，对于现有代码（如deal.II）的模块化可能不如从零开始设计模块化有效，并指出通过其他方法（如pch、forward decls）可能获得更大性能提升。

• trostaft对作者（Wolfgang）及其团队在计算数学和研究软件方面的成就表示赞赏，并期待阅读其作品，显示出对作者专业性的信任和期待。

• nsoonhui提出，LLMs可能有助于将遗留的Fortran或COBOL程序转换为现代语言，认为这种任务应该是LLMs的强项，因为语法和需求明确，且输出可验证。

• barchar指出，模块化主要帮助解析时间，而非代码生成时间，并可能因内联和全局优化的增加而负面影响代码生成性能。他还提到，当依赖项未模块化时，会出现大的全局模块片段，增加BMI大小和解析时间，并指出当前构建系统对头文件单元支持不足的问题。

• Asooka希望看到模块化与预编译头文件的比较，怀疑预编译头文件可能以更少的工作量提供相同的编译时间收益。

• isatty仅对代码块的样式表示不满，未深入讨论技术内容。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及模块化对不同编译阶段的影响，以及当前工具链（如构建系统、编译器）对模块化支持的不足。
• 对于遗留代码的模块化改造和LLMs在代码转换中的潜在应用也有一定的讨论。
• 预编译头文件作为模块化的替代方案被提及，显示出对不同优化方法的权衡和选择的关注。

Computer Science > Software Engineering

Title:
Experience converting a large mathematical software package written in C++ to C++20 modules
Authors:
Wolfgang Bangerth
View a PDF of the paper titled Experience converting a large mathematical software package written in C++ to C++20 modules, by Wolfgang Bangerth
View PDF
Abstract:
Mathematical software has traditionally been built in the form of "packages" that build on each other. A substantial fraction of these packages is written in C++ and, as a consequence, the interface of a package is described in the form of header files that downstream packages and applications can then #include. C++ has inherited this approach towards exporting interfaces from C, but the approach is clunky, unreliable, and slow. As a consequence, C++20 has introduced a "module" system in which packages explicitly export declarations and code that compilers then store in machine-readable form and that downstream users can "import" -- a system in line with what many other programming languages have used for decades.
Herein, I explore how one can convert large mathematical software packages written in C++ to this system, using the
this http URL
finite element library with its around 800,000 lines of code as an example. I describe an approach that allows providing both header-based and module-based interfaces from the same code base, discuss the challenges one encounters, and how modules actually work in practice in a variety of technical and human metrics. The results show that with a non-trivial, but also not prohibitive effort, the conversion to modules is possible, resulting in a reduction in compile time for the converted library itself; on the other hand, for downstream projects, compile times show no clear trend. I end with thoughts about long-term strategies for converting the entire ecosystem of mathematical software over the coming years or decades.

data.title: What should a native DOM templating API look like?
data.author: jdkoeck
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了创建一个声明式JavaScript DOM模板API的设想。该API旨在让开发者描述他们想要的DOM结构，而不是如何实现。它类似于JSX和lit-html等语法，专注于模板的创建和更新，而不涉及组件。这个API必须符合多项约束，如保持网页兼容性、不引入破坏性变化、不影响现有网站性能，以及保持低安全风险。此外，该API应直接可用且易于使用，无需编译器，并与现有JavaScript和DOM平台保持一致。其核心目标是为框架提供一个原始模板功能，使其能够在其上构建组件。关键要求包括API的人体工程学设计和可供JavaScript库内部使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript客户端应用的模板和渲染方案选择，涉及不同的框架和技术，如lit-html、Svelte、React、Signals、VDOM等。

不同观点：
• **支持使用lit-html**：[polyrand]认为lit-html的`html`和`render`函数简单、方便、快速，特别是因为它缓存了渲染部分，状态改变时重新渲染性能也不错。同时，使用Vanilla JS使得组件只是使用`html`模板字符串的函数，易于组合和理解，比React更容易推理。

• **支持Svelte**：[maxloh]提出Svelte的语法更具可读性，并给出示例代码展示Svelte的简洁性。对没有提及Svelte表示不解。

• **支持Tagged Template Literals**：[vlucas]强烈支持使用Tagged Template Literals进行模板渲染，认为这是最简单且原生的JavaScript方案，尤其在与native Signals结合时效果很好。他还提到服务端渲染也主要依赖字符串，因此模板使用字符串是合理且高效的。

• **对模板字符串和AST的讨论**：[bevr1337]认为嵌套函数调用或基于对象的API不够“像HTML”，并讨论了模板字符串和AST处理的挑战，提到函数接收未解析的HTML字符串和已计算的表达式，需要进一步处理。

• **批评设计基于VDOM机制**：[MrJohz]批评该设计没有探索Svelte、Vue Vapor或SolidJS的工作原理，认为其依赖于渲染是廉价操作的假设，并指出信号机制框架（如SolidJS）能更有效地避免不必要的渲染。他还质疑该设计的目标用户和实际应用场景。

• **对属性和事件命名空间的建议**：[svieira]不满意使用不同符号来区分属性、事件等，认为JavaScript不像Perl或K语言，应该采用更符合JavaScript习惯的命名空间方式，如`on:`、`attr:`等。

• **简化框架，避免编译器和属性黑客**：[rglover]认为许多流行框架过于依赖属性黑客和编译器，而直接使用HTML字符串加上一些抽象就能构建出健壮的UI框架，并分享了自己的项目[1]。

补充讨论：
• **对安全性的担忧**：[dvh]强调默认应是安全的，避免像`innerHTML = user_name`这样的字符串拼接，以防止安全漏洞。

• **对模板语言的批评**：[timewizard]最喜欢Amrita模板库，认为将代码和元素混合在一起的模板语言脆弱且难以扩展，提倡将DOM和逻辑分开处理。

• **其他评论**：[hk1337]称赞文章字体大，考虑在自己的博客中效仿。[RadiozRadioz]认为这种方案会像XSLT。

争议焦点：
• **模板字符串 vs. AST/VDOM**：关于模板字符串处理的便捷性与AST处理复杂性之间的争议。
• **不同框架的优劣**：如Svelte的可读性与React/Lit的VDOM机制对比，信号机制框架（如SolidJS）与传统VDOM机制的效率讨论。
• **命名和语法的习惯**：对属性和事件命名空间的符号选择存在不同意见。

44436290.article_content:
If you read my previous post,
The time is right for a DOM templating API
, you might be wondering what such an API would look like.
Let's dive into that question now.
What are we building?
First, let's clarify what we're trying to design here, because when people hear the abstract template API idea described, before there's a concrete proposal or examples, they can sometimes think of very different things.
In
webcomponents/1069
I propose that we add a "declarative JavaScript templating API"
Declarative means that the developer is describing
what
they want, not
how
to achieve it. What exactly constitutes "declarative" is often debatable, and under every declarative API is an imperative implementation, but hopefully people can align on the spirit of the word.
By "templating" we mean the ability to describe the DOM that the developer wants to create and update in a form that resembles the output. This includes syntaxes like JSX and lit-html, which for some people count as something other than templating. For our purposes, they are.
Taken together, "declarative DOM templating" is something that is very, very common. All major frameworks today have declarative templating at their core.
But we're going to narrow our focus a bit
JavaScript
APIs.
By "JavaScript API" we mean methods, classes, etc. that are part of the overall DOM JavaScript API surface. Something that's a sibling and alternative to
innerHTML
,
importNode()
, and a bunch of other DOM APIs that web developers and frameworks use to create and update DOM. But also, we mean that script-like abilities will be left to JavaScript, not added to markup.
It's also important to not that we're not talking about components at all, just templated DOM creation and updating. Most frameworks intertwine the two concepts, so some people aren't aware that there can be a distinction. One of the use cases for this proposal is to be a primitive that frameworks can use, so it's necessary that components can be added on top of templates, but any such feature to do that should be as generic and minimal as possible.
What's guiding us?
In my experience, we can derive the general API shape for this feature from its constraints and requirements, with a dash of opinion about good APIs on top. Listing these helps us see what things must be a certain way vs which things can flex as part of the decision space for the problem.
Constraints
Because we're designing a native DOM API, and not a framework, we have more constraints to deal with. A native API has to work within the current platform, can't break existing sites, and has to be viable within the standards process.
Web compatibility: The proposal can't introduce any breaking changes to the platform.
Standard file types: While a proposal could introduce a new file type just for templates, that's unlikely to make it through the web standards process without incredibly compelling reasons. We'll take using the existing file types as a hard constraint.
Standard JavaScript: It's also possible to try to simultaneously introduce changes to both the DOM and JavaScript, but this is also less likely to succeed because we would be dealing with two separate standards bodies and a much larger overall addition to the platform.
JavaScript is not just a web language anymore, and the JavaScript side would likely have to be useful for non-web use-cases to move forward, dramatically raising the complexity of a proposal.
So we'll also take it as a hard constraint that this API works with today's standard JavaScript.
Low implementation security risk: The proposal should not require drastic and potentially-unsafe HTML parser changes. Implementors are just extremely reluctant to make large HTML parser changes, since they are prime targets for attackers and previous changes (like
<template>
)
did
introduce security bugs.
No performance regressions on existing sites. Slowing down existing sites, or benchmarks like Speedometer, will sink a proposal when it's implemented.
Security: New APIs have a much higher security bar to clear than previous platform changes. They need to be secure by default.
No required compiler: This is not universal, but many web platform maintainers insist that web APIs should be directly usable by developers and not require a compiler to be useful. This does not preclude an API from being a good compile target for alternate syntaxes.
Coherence with the platform. Also not universal, but it will be drastically easier to get a proposal accepted if it's coherent with the existing platform. This would prevent us from introducing a new "better DOM", for instance.
Requirements
Next we need to look at our requirements. What does this proposal have to do to be useful and successful? The actual proposal will need to detail its target use cases, but we can list some requirements now:
Ergonomic API: This API should be nice to use directly for developers.
Usable from JavaScript libraries: Libraries should be able to adopt this API as an internal
44436290.article_summary: 本文讨论了创建一个声明式JavaScript DOM模板API的设想。该API旨在让开发者描述他们想要的DOM结构，而不是如何实现。它类似于JSX和lit-html等语法，专注于模板的创建和更新，而不涉及组件。这个API必须符合多项约束，如保持网页兼容性、不引入破坏性变化、不影响现有网站性能，以及保持低安全风险。此外，该API应直接可用且易于使用，无需编译器，并与现有JavaScript和DOM平台保持一致。其核心目标是为框架提供一个原始模板功能，使其能够在其上构建组件。关键要求包括API的人体工程学设计和可供JavaScript库内部使用。

主要讨论点：JavaScript客户端应用的模板和渲染方案选择，涉及不同的框架和技术，如lit-html、Svelte、React、Signals、VDOM等。

不同观点：
• **支持使用lit-html**：[polyrand]认为lit-html的`html`和`render`函数简单、方便、快速，特别是因为它缓存了渲染部分，状态改变时重新渲染性能也不错。同时，使用Vanilla JS使得组件只是使用`html`模板字符串的函数，易于组合和理解，比React更容易推理。

• **支持Svelte**：[maxloh]提出Svelte的语法更具可读性，并给出示例代码展示Svelte的简洁性。对没有提及Svelte表示不解。

• **支持Tagged Template Literals**：[vlucas]强烈支持使用Tagged Template Literals进行模板渲染，认为这是最简单且原生的JavaScript方案，尤其在与native Signals结合时效果很好。他还提到服务端渲染也主要依赖字符串，因此模板使用字符串是合理且高效的。

• **对模板字符串和AST的讨论**：[bevr1337]认为嵌套函数调用或基于对象的API不够“像HTML”，并讨论了模板字符串和AST处理的挑战，提到函数接收未解析的HTML字符串和已计算的表达式，需要进一步处理。

• **批评设计基于VDOM机制**：[MrJohz]批评该设计没有探索Svelte、Vue Vapor或SolidJS的工作原理，认为其依赖于渲染是廉价操作的假设，并指出信号机制框架（如SolidJS）能更有效地避免不必要的渲染。他还质疑该设计的目标用户和实际应用场景。

• **对属性和事件命名空间的建议**：[svieira]不满意使用不同符号来区分属性、事件等，认为JavaScript不像Perl或K语言，应该采用更符合JavaScript习惯的命名空间方式，如`on:`、`attr:`等。

• **简化框架，避免编译器和属性黑客**：[rglover]认为许多流行框架过于依赖属性黑客和编译器，而直接使用HTML字符串加上一些抽象就能构建出健壮的UI框架，并分享了自己的项目[1]。

data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者对芝加哥联邦储备银行货币博物馆中一个声称装有100万美元的透明立方体感到怀疑，并亲自尝试计数验证。通过详细计算，作者发现该立方体实际包含约1,550,400美元，比标示的多出550,400美元。作者解释了计数过程的困难，并为此开发了一个简单的网络工具“Dot Counter”来帮助计数。文章还探讨了可能的解释，包括数学误差、通货膨胀影响以及立方体可能为空心。最终，作者幽默地指出，虽然立方体确实包含100万美元，但也附带了550,400美元的“额外奖金”。

不同观点：
• **[mrandish]** 认为立方体可能只有100万美元，设计者可能为了视觉效果或因计算错误而将立方体做得过大。他建议通过实验验证所需空间。
• **[red_admiral]** 以经济学家式的幽默建议用110万美元购买该立方体，并打赌可以建造另一个类似的立方体还有盈余，以此验证实际金额。
• **[goodcanadian]** 认为更可能是正好100万美元（误差在几个百分比内），并质疑立方体装有超额50万美元的说法，认为是包装不均匀导致视觉误差。
• **[ticulatedspline]** 分析展览设计要求，认为立方体需要满足大、百万美元、整齐堆叠三个条件，并推测立方体可能有空隙或不规则的空隙。
• **[kevin_thibedeau]** 提出隐藏在铝框后面的额外钞票堆，认为这样可以解释立方体容纳更多金额。
• **[ehsankia]** 认为标题有误导性，讨论如果是少了50万会更严重，并认为作为艺术品，大多数人能接受这种不精确。
• **[somat]** 从数学角度讨论立方体尺寸与钞票尺寸的关系，尝试计算最接近百万美元的立方体。
• **[Scarblac]** 简单指出，如果立方体包含150万美元，那么它也包含100万美元，不认为这是个问题。
• **[rkagerer]** 建议在展览旁边放置一个小牌匾，解释这个项目，增加教育意义。
• **[crazysim]** 猜测钞票可能有标记或经过人工处理，用于展示目的。
• **[giancarlostoro]** 质疑立方体中间是否全是钞票，还是存在填充物。
• **[citizenpaul]** 在另一个讨论中涉及联邦工作人员的效率问题，指出美联储 technically 不是政府机构。
• **[pjs_]** 提到一篇关于烧毁百万英镑的文章，与当前讨论略有关联。
• **[nyeah]** 质疑展览是否声称钞票填满整个立方体。
• **[Brian_K_White]** 讨论展示目的，认为无论是多于或少于实际金额，都是不合理的，并推测可能是简单错误或者有其他深层含义。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于立方体是否真的包含150万美元，或者是否存在空隙和填充物。
• 讨论中多次提到立方体的视觉效果和实际金额的差异，以及设计者可能的意图和错误。
• 有人建议通过实验或进一步调查验证实际金额。

data.title: Show HN: HackerNewt – Breadth-first exploring HN client for iOS
data.author: hnand
data.article_summary: HackerNewt是一款第三方Hacker News客户端，通过独特的评论树展示方式，解决传统界面评论过窄和层级不清的问题。其优点包括：评论宽度保持不变、始终显示当前评论的父评论、通过滑动控制子树浏览，以及轻松跳过不感兴趣的子树。此外，应用还提供自定义板块、搜索、阅读列表等功能，提升阅读体验。不过，部分用户反馈应用曾出现加载问题，但开发者迅速修复。该应用不隶属于Hacker News官网，隐私保护良好，免费下载但包含内购。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Hacker News的第三方应用及其功能改进建议

不同观点：
• goodburb建议添加一个持久保存的过滤功能，用于过滤特定话题（如政治或AI），并提到目前使用的替代工具。
• pvg引用了2年前的一个相关讨论，暗示该问题或类似功能建议早已存在。
• eviks对评论区设计中的视觉固定问题提出了看法，认为通过减少空白可以解决部分宽度问题，但对整体设计表示理解和支持。
• krishnasangeeth提到自己曾开发过类似应用，并分享了其应用链接，指出其应用风格与官网相似，且包含一些独特的交互设计。
• afro88对应用的发布表示赞赏，解决了其在HN使用中遇到的问题（如评论折叠不便），但也提到遇到了列表项重复的bug。
• thebruce87m将该应用与HACK进行比较，表达了对HACK长期存在崩溃问题的失望，暗示可能考虑切换应用。
• vrighter对应用的创新性提出质疑，认为其设计类似于默认折叠的树状视图，要求进一步解释差异。
• xp84表示已经使用了该应用的早期版本，并对替代方案的出现表示欢迎，感谢社区开发者的贡献。
• vinnski对应用的简洁设计表示赞赏，但对滑动操作不太习惯，同时对应用中的触感反馈功能表示肯定。
• recov提到应用在刷新 feeds 时较慢的问题，怀疑是HN本身的问题而非应用问题。
• sneak对应用不监控用户数据表示感谢，并提到已购买高级版本以支持开发者。
• fraXis询问是否会发布Android版本，显示了对跨平台支持的关注。
• mittermayr对应用的付费模式提出批评，认为通过限制基础功能（如暗黑模式）来收费不太合理，建议通过独特功能来吸引用户付费。
• ashish01提到自己实现了BFS扩展评论的功能，并分享了一个支持暗黑模式的网页应用链接。
• vednig提到自己也在React Native上开发了一个类似应用，暗示该领域开发者较多且方案多样。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：应用的创新性及付费模式。vrighter质疑应用的创新性，而mittermayr则批评了付费模式的不合理性。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：用户对HN现有问题的反馈（如afro88提到的bug及recov提到的刷新速度问题），以及跨平台支持和暗黑模式的需求（fraXis和ashish01的评论）。

44435211.article_content:
iPhone Screenshots
Description
Don't get lost in big Hacker News discussions!
HackerNewt is a Hacker News client that uses an alternative way of displaying comment tree. Advantages over traditional interfaces:
- Comment width doesn't get narrower no matter how deep in the tree you are
- You always see the parent of the comment you're currently reading
- Swiping allows you to move in and out of subtrees with animated transitions that you fully control
- You can easily skip subtrees that don't interest you by simply scrolling
As a result it's easier to maintain the context and to keep track of where you are in the Hacker News discussion tree. There are also: custom boards, search, in-thread search, anchors, reading list, recent items. Enjoy your Hacker News reading experience!
Developer is not affiliated with Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/) in any way.

data.title: Graph Theory Applications in Video Games
data.author: haywirez
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了Clara Nguyễn关于图论在电子游戏中应用的演讲内容。演讲涵盖了图论的基本概念及其在游戏开发中的实际应用，包括：3D图形的顶点和边如何在图形中表示和处理，赛车游戏中的圈数计算，利用并查集生成迷宫，以及bitDP理论的应用等。演讲还讨论了1982年Atari 2600游戏《Entombed》中的一个未解问题。演讲时长为60-75分钟，内容深入，并包含与听众的互动。文章还提供了几个技术性问题及其答案，以帮助听众理解演讲内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Graph Theory在视频游戏中的应用及其具体实现方法

不同观点：
• [j2kun] 认为Graph Theory在视频游戏中的应用不仅仅限于理论，有许多实际应用，例如在视频游戏中的路径寻找等。然而，他指出文章中提到的某些应用似乎更偏向于假设性，缺乏实际使用证据。虽然作者没有提供这些技术在游戏设计中被实际应用的证明，但[j2kun]仍然肯定了作者提出这些想法的贡献，只是认为标题和引言具有误导性。

• [Llamamoe] 指出文章遗漏了图形语法（graph grammar）在关卡生成中的应用，特别是由游戏Unexplored首创的关卡生成算法。他认为这是一种非常吸引人的程序化生成（procgen）算法，值得讨论。

• [palmfacehn] 强调了在大型房间和走廊网络中寻找路径的明显应用，认为这是Graph Theory在游戏中的一个直接而实用的例子。

Talk Summary & Table of Contents
Graph Theory isn't just a topic that is restricted to being
"theory". There are several real-life applications of it. One of
those just happens to be video games. In this talk, I go over a
brief overview of several concepts where Graph Theory is applied.
The topics covered vary a bit:
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
-
Vertices in 3D space, how they are represented, and the
"rules" of dealing with vertices and edges.
Race Games & Lap Counting
-
Racing games where circuits are used to count laps, as
well as a mention of
Mario Kart Wii
and its Ultra-Shortcuts, to encourage
the simplicity of Hamiltonian Circuit checking for lap
counting.
Maze Generation w/ Disjoint-Sets & Union-Find
-
I talk about how to generate mazes efficiently, as well as
taking it a step up. Generation of multiple connected mazes
along with multi-floor/dimensional mazes are described. The
true power of the Disjoint-Set data structure with
optimisations is also discussed in depth.
bitDP, a theoretical approach
-
As a bonus, a theoretical "Part 2" to
my bitDP talk
is
included too. I talk about the theory behind it and how it
can be applied to a game to optimally guarantee that a
Hamiltonian Path exists in a generated graph.
Entombed (1982 Atari 2600 game)
-
For an added bonus, I also discuss an unsolved problem
involving an Atari 2600 game,
Entombed
.
Just a heads up, this talk is
60-75 minutes long
. Concepts
will be discussed in great depth. However, the talk was
intentionally constructed for me to be over-prepared, with topics
that can be skipped if I do not have time to cover everything. As
such, I link to this page in the slides if anyone is interested in
the full talk. Audience interaction is welcome mid-talk. In the
event that I skip topics, the questions below are guaranteed to be
covered while I'm talking.

What does bitDP stand for?
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
Most graphs discussed in our Graph Theory are abstract and may be
visualised in any way as long as it follows a set of rules.
Likewise, in computer graphics, there are "rules" too. However,
they are quite different from the theoretical graph theory we are
used to discussing. How a vertex and an edge are percived are
different and absolute.
Here's a few rules:
Vertices have
positional
coordinates (x, y, z) to
define position in space. Consequently, this means that
there is only
one
way to represent them in space.
Edges (connections between vertices) are
implied
,
based on a drawing mode of the programmer's choice. They

go over them below.
Everything is oriented around
triangles

you wanted to make a square, you do it with two triangles.
If you wanted to make a curved surface, you have to

We have three dimensions to work with here. The coordinates are

When we draw a triangle, it's filled, obviously. However, only one

due to

. The side that gets drawn depends

data.article_summary: 文章探讨了自然界中色彩和色觉的演化历史，提出了一个类似“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题：究竟是鲜艳的色彩信号先出现，还是识别这些色彩的色觉先演化出来？科学家Zachary Emberts和John Wiens通过研究化石记录和系统发育树，重建了5亿年的演化历史。他们发现，色彩信号和色觉可能是共同演化的。色彩信号用于吸引配偶、诱导传粉等，而色觉则帮助识别这些信号。尽管有些生物丧失了部分色觉能力，但色彩在演化过程中持续存在，表明其传递信息的益处超过了吸引捕食者的风险。文章还提到，像蜥蜴这样的动物通过色彩信号传递健康信息，而色彩和色觉的演化是一个复杂且相互关联的过程。

When Did Nature Burst Into Vivid Color?
By

Scientists reconstructed 500 million years of evolutionary history to reveal which came first: colorful signals or the color vision needed to see them.

The natural world is awash with color, and many of these vibrant hues are meant to be seen. Apples blush red to coax animals to spread their seeds, lavender blooms are violet to lure in pollinating bees, and male peacocks trailed by flashy blue trains more successfully attract mates.
However, the world is colorful only for some of us. These vivid signals can be perceived by animals that can see in color; to organisms that have limited or no color vision, many of these bright colors don’t mean anything at all. This raises interesting evolutionary questions. Which came first: colorful signals or the color vision needed to see them? And when did these optical signals emerge and take off, painting the natural world in the kaleidoscopic spectrum we see today?
“Some birds are red, some snakes are red, and some plants have red fruits. In each of these cases, the red coloration serves as a signal,” said
Zachary Emberts
, an evolutionary biologist at Oklahoma State University. “This led us to wonder: What was the initial function of conspicuous coloration, like red, and color vision?”
Emberts and his former postdoctoral adviser
John Wiens
, an evolutionary ecologist at the University of Arizona, combed through research encompassing hundreds of millions of years of evolutionary history to offer a scientific answer to the
chicken-and-egg question of color
. The researchers used the fossil record and phylogenetic trees — timelines of species emergence that are based largely on modern traits — to infer when colorful signals may have first emerged in plants and animals. Then they tested their hypothesis that color vision and colorful signals evolved together.
“What I love about this paper is the ambition and confidence to pursue big questions and explore ideas that will inevitably involve speculation,” said
William Allen
, an ecologist who studies sensory systems at Swansea University in Wales and was not involved in the new study. “There is a tendency for science in the 21st century to focus on applying analytic techniques to data, and this can sometimes be at the detriment to deep thought, natural history and curiosity.”
The Evolution of Color
As a graduate student at the University of Texas, Austin, Wiens was fascinated by pretty animals. For his dissertation, he studied blue-bellied lizards, which have earth-toned backs and sapphire undersides, to examine how sexual signaling might have evolved. He built a phylogenetic tree of lizard species and was fascinated to see that the males’ blue patches, which signal fitness to females,
frequently disappeared and reappeared
along the evolutionary timeline, perhaps because females stopped picking up on the signals in some lineages. That project piqued his interest in how the production and recognition of color signals might have evolved.

As a graduate student, John Wiens first encountered colored patches used by lizards as a sexual signal. Decades later, he resumed his exploration of the use of color by organisms.
Ramona Walls
There are some costs to color. For example, a vivid signal to attract a mate may attract predators as well. But the persistence of color throughout evolutionary history suggests that, for many organisms, the information it communicates is beneficial enough to outweigh the cost. However, without color vision, the value of maintaining distinctive coloration would vanish; indeed, there would be little reason for it to evolve in the first place. That made Wiens wonder why different species evolved the ability to see color — perhaps to find colorful fruit, flowers or mates? Did those palettes even exist at the time?
Some components of color vision have been lost over evolutionary time.

• **quantadev**：认为计算机器人数量没有实际意义，关注未来是否会出现由机器人完全运营的大型企业，但指出 humanoid 机器人并非工业应用的理想选择，未来自动化更多依赖无形的人工智能。
• **turnsout**：调侃全民基本收入（UBI）未实现，暗示社会应对自动化带来的失业问题准备不足。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：自动化是否会导致大规模失业及其社会后果。Henchman21和malfist表达了对失业和社会动荡的担忧，而djoldman和quantadev更关注技术效率和未来发展的可能性。
• **论据和例子**：dogleash提供了非自动化工具同样减少人力需求的例子，quantadev则讨论了未来人工智能无形态的自动化趋势。
• **社会和经济影响**：评论中多次提到自动化对就业市场和社会结构的潜在影响，反映了人们对技术进步带来的经济和社会变化的广泛关注。

data.title: All Good Editors Are Pirates: In Memory of Lewis H. Lapham
data.author: Caiero
data.article_summary: 这篇文章纪念了美国散文家兼编辑刘易斯·H·拉普姆（Lewis H. Lapham），他于2024年7月23日去世。作者聚焦于与刘易斯共事的时光，特别是拉普姆季刊（Lapham’s Quarterly）的创立过程。2007年，刘易斯在纽约曼哈顿创办该杂志，办公室里充满了书籍和知识的气息。作者作为首位全职编辑加入，见证了杂志从无到有，逐渐发展到拥有四万订阅者和年度盛会的过程。刘易斯工作勤奋，每期杂志的开篇文章都精心打磨，多次修改。他平易近人，乐于听取每个人的意见，尽管他出身名门，却常讽刺美国统治阶级。作者回忆起与刘易斯共度的时光，包括在酒吧讨论杂志内容和设计的夜晚，对他充满敬佩与怀念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Lewis Lapham的纪念及其相关话题的讨论，包括其作品、编辑理念以及创意与抄袭的界限。

不同观点：
• [skadamou] 分享了多个关于Lewis Lapham的悼念文章链接，引导读者去不同来源了解Lapham的生平和影响。
• [svara] 对Lapham的播客《The World in Time》给予高度评价，认为Lapham像是来自另一个时代的人物，强调其独特性。
• [PostOnce] 被文章顶部的图片吸引，引发对舞台设计模型和微缩模型的研究兴趣，偏离了原本对Lapham的讨论。
• [ggm] 提到Robertson Davies和E. Anne Proulx曾用小镇报纸编辑为主题进行写作，可能暗示Lapham的编辑风格与这些作家的文学主题有相似之处。
• [Aachen] 引用了文章中的一句话，指出Lapham认为“所有优秀的编辑都是海盗”，他们从每个人那里偷取灵感，以此解释编辑的创造性过程。

• 评论中对Lapham作为编辑和创作者的角色有较多讨论，特别是他的“海盗”理念，即编辑需要从各种来源获取灵感，引发了对创意过程的深入探讨。

Wikimedia Commons

This remembrance first appeared in
Stranger’s Guide
on July 28, 2024.
O
n July 23, 2024, the American essayist and editor Lewis H. Lapham died. Since then several beautiful obituaries have been written about the great man and I won’t attempt to repeat these, though I certainly encourage reading them. Instead I want to focus on a very particular time and place where I worked with Lewis and knew him best—the book-filled offices of his last great project,
Lapham’s Quarterly
.
After a storied tenure of nearly thirty years at
Harper’s Magazine
, Lewis founded
Lapham’s Quarterly
in 2007 as a magazine of the history of ideas. The offices were housed on Irving Place just off Union Square in Manhattan. Here I spent eight years as executive editor and found the offices to be a magical place filled with knowledge, wit, history, literature, and cigarette smoke. In those book-lined rooms I got an up-close lesson on how to start a magazine and how to run it with grace. It’s also where I met Abby Rapoport,
Stranger’s Guide
’s publisher and my co-founder as we built our own magazine years later.
Back in 2007 I was the first full-time editorial hire Lewis made. On my first day of work, I was greeted by the only other staff members in the office. The first was Ann Gollin, Lewis’ rock and longtime assistant. The second was a young intern in flip-flops and cut-off shorts. That was it, that was the entire operation. There was no website, no magazine, no subscribers. Instead there was just the beginning of Lewis’ idea that we cull through the great books and create a digest of thought and ideas. Each issue would be on a new theme, be it war, religion, or food.
When I left eight years later, Lewis had built a thriving magazine with forty thousand subscribers and an annual gala—the Decades Ball—headlined by the likes of Tom Hanks and Anne Hathaway. There was a robust intellectual editorial board that met four times a year around a large wooden table to discuss
Thucydides
,
Marx
, or
Hannah Arendt
.
But that all came later. On that very first day of work, Lewis took me out, first to a party at André Schiffrin’s penthouse apartment, where he introduced me to
Joan Didion
before slipping out to a late dinner at Elaine’s. Here we sat at what Lewis assured me was the best table in the house. Within minutes the grande dame herself, Elaine, plopped down at our table with a tremendous sigh, as if we were just the port in the storm she’d been waiting for. An endless stream of people dropped by to say hello or to drink or to argue politics late into the night. I was accustomed to a very different crowd—those of small leftist magazines and the New School philosophy graduate students.
“Where am I?” I wondered. “What have I just signed on to?”
When Lewis founded
Lapham’s Quarterly
, he had already been inducted into the American Society of Magazine Editors Hall of Fame. He was already famous as an essayist, editor, and author of countless books. But despite all his accolades, those early days at
Lapham’s Quarterly
had the feel of a 1940s movie about a plucky team of actors putting on a show, a kind of “Gee shucks folks, let’s make a magazine!” On Lewis’ desk, next to the ashtrays and the blue folders full of notes, sat the book
How to Start a Magazine
, which was hurriedly tucked away the day the
New York Times
came to photograph the offices. In those days, I was married to the magazine’s art director and we didn’t yet have kids. So almost every evening after work we’d head off for drinks with Lewis at the nearby bar, Paul & Jimmy’s, where Lewis quickly established himself as a regular. It was here we spent countless hours discussing this nascent publication, its cover, the printer, the feel of an issue, and ideas for themes and authors.
Lewis was an incessantly hard worker; he was the first to arrive at the office and the last to leave. Almost every night after work he’d head off to a dinner, a book party, or some other glamorous literary event. Although he was already in his seventies, I never saw a man work harder.
Each issue of
Lapham’s Quarterly
opened with an essay by Lewis that he would painstakingly labor over for weeks; seventeen drafts for one essay was not uncommon. Ann Gollin, his trusty accomplice in all things great and small, would diligently transcribe the essays he dictated on a small hand-held tape recorder. And then she’d transcribe them again, then yet again, as he crafted and re-crafted each sentence.
Lewis would show everyone in the office his drafts, from the interns to the publisher, asking eagerly, “What do you think?” He looked for ideas and input everywhere. He was never an elitist even though he summered in Newport, his pocket squares were crisp, and his cufflinks shined. Lewis’ essays poked fun at the American ruling class from his position within the belly of the beast.
