data.title: Sliding Window Technique Visualizer
data.author: neumannbd
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种用于理解和可视化滑动窗口技术的工具，支持固定和可变窗口大小。固定窗口大小用于如寻找大小为k的子数组最大和或计算移动平均值等问题；可变窗口大小则用于寻找满足特定条件的最优子数组，如最长含有k个不同字符的子串。文中提供了多种常见应用场景和不同编程语言的代码实现示例，并展示了时间与空间复杂度分析。用户可以通过输入数组和参数进行可视化操作，理解滑动窗口技术在不同问题中的应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：滑动窗口算法的高效性及其可视化

不同观点：
• **Materialpoint 的观点：** 
  - 他认为滑动窗口算法，尤其是固定窗口大小的情况下，应该通过增加新元素并减去最旧元素来更新运行中的总和，从而实现O(1)的运行时间（除初始化成本外）。
  - 他提到了Perreault和Hébert的“恒定时间中值滤波”以及Weiss的“快速中值和双边滤波”作为高效实现的例子，尤其在图像处理中的应用。
  - 对可视化工具没有清晰解释这一点表示不满。

• **Dvdhs 的观点：**
  - 认为该可视化工具并没有展示滑动窗口算法的有用部分，将其视为“AI slop”（指低质量或不清晰的内容），质疑其实际效果。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点：** 
  - 争议的核心在于滑动窗口算法的效率和可视化工具的有效性。Materialpoint关注算法的实现细节及其时间复杂度，尤其是如何通过增加和减少元素来维持O(1)的效率；而Dvdhs则认为可视化工具没有充分展示算法的关键点，质疑其教学或展示价值。
  
• **具体例子：**
  - Materialpoint引用了具体的学术工作（Perreault和Hébert的中值滤波，Weiss的快速中值和双边滤波）来支持其对滑动窗口算法高效性的理解。
  
• **对可视化工具的批评：**
  - 两位评论者都对可视化工具表示不满，但出发点不同。Materialpoint希望看到更详细的算法实现细节，而Dvdhs则认为整个工具没有展示算法的核心价值。

data.title: PlanetScale for Postgres
data.author: adocomplete
data.article_summary: 2025年7月1日，PlanetScale宣布推出私密预览版**PlanetScale for Postgres**，号称是全球最快的Postgres托管平台。该平台响应客户需求，旨在解决当前Postgres托管平台常见的宕机、性能差和成本高的问题。PlanetScale for Postgres使用真实Postgres运行于其专有操作器上，提供高可用性、自动故障转移、查询缓冲和连接池等功能，并支持无停机自动更新Postgres版本。此外，PlanetScale Metal的本地NVMe SSD驱动器显著改善了云中托管关系数据库的性能/成本比。虽然Vitess是PlanetScale的强项，但为了适应Postgres，正在从头构建新系统，未来将提供更多信息和早期访问机会。公司邀请运行大规模Postgres的企业参与合作。感兴趣者可注册私密预览等候名单。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PlanetScale 推出 PostgreSQL 服务的评价和讨论

不同观点：
• joshstrange：他从 PlanetScale 转向了 Neon，因为 PlanetScale 不支持每个租户一个数据库，而且需要为每个数据库支付高额费用。他的使用场景是小规模、自筹资金的公司，负载波动大但可预测。他认为 Neon 更适合他的需求，但仍然对 PlanetScale 抱有期待，并赞赏其产品和支持服务。

• kellysutton：作为一名使用 PlanetScale MySQL 两年的用户，他认为这是 PostgreSQL 社区的一个令人兴奋的消息。他将使用 PlanetScale 的体验比作从 Treo 手机升级到 iPhone，认为其在各个方面都更优秀，并祝贺 PlanetScale 团队。

• ezekg：他提到最近 PostgreSQL 的扩展和缩放技术发展，期待 PlanetScale 的进一步信息，并表示会持续关注。

• simonw：他关注 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 服务是否与 Vitess 有技术传承，并自行找到答案，确认这是从零开始构建的新系统。

• rtyu1120：他质疑为什么 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 在 Amazon EBS 上的表现被排除在基准测试之外，认为没有这一部分的基准测试显得不完整。

• samlambert：作为 PlanetScale 的代表，他表示团队在推出 PostgreSQL 产品过程中非常享受，并愿意回答任何问题。

• brycethornton：他认为更多/更好的竞争托管 PostgreSQL 服务是有益的，期待看到 Supabase 的 Multigres 与 PlanetScale 的对比。

• rodolphoarruda：他离题提到 PlanetScale 网站上的一个 MySQL 开发者课程，认为这是一个亮点。

• wasd：他祝贺 PlanetScale 的发布，并询问 PostgreSQL 扩展的可用性及其限制。

• ff4：他对 PlanetScale 转向 PostgreSQL 的技术挑战表示关注，特别是数据分片和分布式系统的复杂性，并建议让 Jepsen 这样的第三方来评估其一致性和功能损失。

补充讨论：
• 技术传承和创新：simonw 和官方回应（samlambert）提到了 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 服务是从零开始构建的新系统，而非基于 Vitess 的技术。
• 竞争和对比：brycethornton 和 joshstrange 提到了与 Neon 和 Supabase 的竞争，并期待看到更多的对比和信息。
• 性能和基准测试：rtyu1120 质疑基准测试的完整性，特别是 Amazon EBS 部分的缺失。
• 功能和扩展性：wasd 和 ff4 关注 PostgreSQL 扩展的可用性及其在分布式系统中的表现和限制。

Announcing PlanetScale for Postgres
By
Sam Lambert
|
July 1, 2025
Today we are announcing the private preview of PlanetScale for Postgres: the worldâs fastest Postgres hosting platform.
You can request access to PlanetScale for Postgres by visiting this
link
.
We are already hosting customers' production workloads with incredible results.
Convex
, the complete backend solution for app developers, is migrating their reactive database infrastructure to PlanetScale for Postgres. Read more about their migration
here
.
Never say never
PlanetScale has been successful hosting some of the worldâs largest relational databases, so why are we building for Postgres? The reason is simple: customer demand. In March we announced
PlanetScale Metal
and something wild happened. We had an immense number of companies reaching out to us asking us to support Postgres. The demand was so overwhelming that by the end of launch day we knew we had to do this. We are nothing without our customers, we do the difficult but boring bit of providing industry leading uptime so they can build incredible products. We want more and more exciting companies building on PlanetScale.
Performance and reliability
Our initial goal was to convince ourselves we could be additive to the ecosystem and provide something of value. We spoke to over 50 customers of the current Postgres hosting platforms and we heard identical stories of regular outages, poor performance, and high cost. PlanetScale is an engineering company. We are not going to enter a market with anything but exceptional engineering.
We had to validate we could out-perform the current solutions while being more reliable. This led us to building a
comprehensive benchmark methodology
. After extensive testing we are proud to share that we consistently outperform every Postgres product on the market, even when giving the competition 2x the resources:
Amazon Aurora
AlloyDB
Lakebase/Neon
Supabase
Heroku
Crunchy Data
TigerData
PlanetScale for Postgres uses real Postgres running on our proprietary operator meaning we can bring the maturity of PlanetScale and the performance of Metal to an even wider audience. Todayâs release already achieves true high availability with automatic failovers, query buffering, and connection pooling via our proprietary proxy layer PSBouncer. We run Postgres v17 and support online imports from any version > Postgres v13, as well as automatic Postgres version updates without downtime. Additionally, PlanetScale Metalâs locally-attached NVMe SSD drives fundamentally change the performance/cost ratio for hosting relational databases in the cloud. Weâre excited to bring this performance to Postgres.
Vitess for Postgres
Vitess is one of PlanetScaleâs greatest strengths and has become synonymous with database scaling. Contemporary Vitess is the product of PlanetScaleâs experience running at extreme scale. We have made explicit sharding accessible to hundreds of thousands of users and it is time to bring this power to Postgres. We will not however be using Vitess to do this.
Vitessâ achievements are enabled by leveraging MySQLâs strengths and engineering around its weaknesses. To achieve Vitessâ power for Postgres we are architecting from first principles. We are well under way with building this new system and will be releasing more information and early access as we progress. As with all PlanetScale products we work with customers at scale to build and validate maturity. If your company runs Postgres at a significant scale and this is something that interests you,
reach out

data.title: Types of Types: Common to Exotic
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Lean语言中的类型系统，包括四种基本类型：函数类型（Pi类型）、积类型、和类型（归纳类型）以及商类型。Lean采用三级结构：宇宙（如Type、Prop）、类型（宇宙的元素）和项（类型的元素）。类型用于分类项并规定其使用规则，而宇宙避免了如罗素悖论等悖论。简单类型如自然数（nat）和布尔值（bool）是基础，可以构建复杂类型如函数类型（α → β）和积类型（α × β）。

函数类型可以是依赖或非依赖的，依赖函数类型用Π表示。积类型组合多个值，结构体是其示例。和类型表示选择，如不同形状的面积计算。商类型表示在某种关系下等价的值。依赖类型允许类型依赖于值，如向量长度作为类型的一部分。差分类型通过依赖类型和证明义务编码，用于表达"类型A中去掉满足属性B的元素"。

Lean使用#check命令检查表达式的类型，帮助验证类型正确性。通过这些类型，Lean实现了丰富的类型系统，支持复杂的数学和逻辑建模。

44435805.article_content:
Types of Types: Common â Exotic
Programming languages offer various ways to model data through their type systems. Let's explore these concepts using Lean, which has a particularly rich type system supporting four fundamental kinds of types: function types (Pi types), product types, sum types (inductive types), and quotient types. In Lean, mathematical objects exist in a three-level hierarchy:
Universes
(e.g.,
Type
,
Prop
)
Types
(elements of universes)
Terms
(elements of types)
A
type
is a term of a universe (like
Type
or
Prop
) that classifies other terms and enforces computational and logical rules about how they can be used. A
term
is a mathematical object that has a unique type, denoted using
:
(e.g.,
37 : â
means 37 is a term of type real numbers). This forms a strict hierarchy: terms are elements of types, and types are themselves terms of universes, but to avoid paradoxes like Russell's, there is no "type of all types" - instead, we have an infinite hierarchy of universes.
In Lean, simple types are foundational and include basic types like
nat
for natural numbers and
bool
for booleans. These types are first-class citizens, meaning they can be manipulated and passed around just like any other data. Lean's type system allows for the construction of complex types from these simple ones, such as function types (
Î± â Î²
) and product types (
Î± Ã Î²
).
The
#check
command in Lean is a powerful tool used to query the type of an expression. It helps verify the types of constants, functions, and expressions, ensuring they conform to expected types. For example:
constant m : nat    -- m is a natural number
constant n : nat    -- n is a natural number
#check m            -- output: nat
#check n + 0        -- nat
#check tt           -- boolean "true"
While set theory uses
â
for membership, type theory uses
:
to denote that a term has a particular type:
-- In set theory: 37 â â
-- In type theory:
#check 37 : â        -- 37 is a term of type â
#check â : Type      -- â is a term of type Type
To avoid
Russell's Paradox
, there isn't a type of all types. Instead, we have universes:
Type
: Universe containing mathematical objects (e.g.,
â
,
â
, groups, rings)
Prop
: Universe containing propositions (true/false statements)
For types
X
and
Y
, the type of functions from
X
to
Y
is written
X â Y
:
def square : â â â := Î» x, x^2
#check square        -- â â â
The famous
Curry-Howard correspondence
states:
Propositions are types in
Prop
Proofs are terms of these types
True propositions have exactly one term
False propositions have zero terms
-- P â Q represents both:
-- 1. A function type from proofs of P to proofs of Q
-- 2. The logical implication P implies Q
Function types
, also known as
Pi types
, represent mappings between types. They can either be dependent or non-dependent. For example:
-- Simple function type (non-dependent)
def square : â â â := Î» x, x^2
-- Dependent function type (Pi type)
def vector_length : Î  (n : Nat), Vector â n â â
| 0 _ := 0
| (n+1) v := real.sqrt (dot_product v v)
The Pi type notation
Î  (x : A), B x
represents a dependent function type where the return type
B x
can depend on the input value
x
. When the return type doesn't depend on the input, we use the simpler arrow notation
A â B
.
Product types
represent combinations of multiple values:
structure Point :=
(x : Int)
(y : Int)
structure Person :=
(name : String)
(age : Int)
(address : String)
Sum types
, also known as
inductive types
, represent alternatives:
inductive Shape
| circle (radius : Float)
| rectangle (width : Float) (height : Float)
| triangle (base : Float) (height : Float)
-- Example of using the equation compiler with sum types
def area : Shape â Float
| Shape.circle r := Float.pi * r * r
| Shape.rectangle w h := w * h
| Shape.triangle b h := b * h / 2
Quotient types
represent values that are equivalent under some relation:
-- Define an equivalence relation for angles
def angle_equiv (a b : Float) : Prop :=
â k : Int, a = b + k * 360
-- Create a quotient type for angles mod 360
def Angle := quotient (setoid.mk angle_equiv)
-- Constructor for angles
def mk_angle (degrees : Float) : Angle :=
quotient.mk degrees
Dependent types
allow types to depend on values:
-- A vector type whose length is part of its type
inductive Vector (Î± : Type) : Nat â Type
| nil : Vector Î± 0
| cons : Î± â {n : Nat} â Vector Î± n â Vector Î± (n + 1)
-- A function whose return type depends on its input
def get_type (b : Bool) : Type :=
if b then Nat else String
Difference types
represent the "subtraction" of one type from another. While not directly supported in Lean, we can encode them using dependent types and proof obligations. They're particularly useful when we want to express "Type A without elements satisfying property B."
-- Non-zero numbers: â "minus" 0
def NonZero := {x : â // x â  0}
-- Non-empty lists: List Î± "minus" empty list
def NonEmptyList (Î± : Type) :=

The GIST

by

, 																								reviewed by

Credit: Unsplash/CC0 Public Domain
People with higher levels of trust—in both others and institutions—report higher levels of subjective well-being, an important indicator of quality of life and predictor of health and longevity, than those with lower levels of trust, according to research published in
Psychological Bulletin
.
The study, "
Trust and Subjective Well-Being Across the Lifespan: A Multilevel Meta-Analysis of Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Associations
," also found that well-being and trust reinforce each other over time.
"Our findings show that trust plays a key role in how happy and satisfied people feel across all ages, especially so for children, adolescents and older adults. Whether it's trust in others, in society or in institutions, all types matter for well-being," said Catrin Finkenauer, Ph.D., a professor at Utrecht University and a co-author of the study.
Subjective well-being is different from other types of well-being in that it focuses on how people feel about their own lives rather than on external factors like
physical health
, wealth or education, and it is generally measured using self-reports.
To better understand the relationship between trust and well-being, researchers conducted a
meta-analysis
of existing research, comprising nearly 1,000 findings from studies involving over 2.5 million participants, ages 6 to 84 years, from around the world.
The most commonly studied countries were the United States (43 studies), China (37) and the United Kingdom (19). The research looked at three types of individual-level trust (interpersonal, institutional and generalized), as well as a variety of well-being indicators.
"Well-being in our study includes both emotional experiences, like how often someone feels happy or sad, or whether they report anxiety or
depressive symptoms
, and more reflective judgments, like whether they feel satisfied with their life overall," said co-author Marlies Maes, Ph.D., assistant professor at Utrecht University.
The team of researchers found that people who trust more, whether it's trust in others, in institutions or in society in general, tended to feel happier and more satisfied with life than people who trust less.
Trust is the glue that holds relationships, communities and societies together. Research shows that supportive, healthy relationships are key to well-being—and trust plays a central role in building and maintaining those connections. This may help explain why people who trust others and institutions tend to report higher levels of well-being, according to Finkenauer.
Several of the analyzed studies were longitudinal, allowing the researchers to track changes over time. These revealed a clear pattern: Trust boosted well-being, and people who felt better about their lives also tended to become more trusting over time.
"In today's world, where media can both connect and mislead, safeguarding
public trust
is more important than ever," said Finkenauer. "By promoting media literacy and enacting fair regulations, we take essential steps to protect that trust."
"But trust can't be forced—it has to be earned," she said. "Families, schools and governments all share the responsibility of creating environments where people can rely on each other. When we build trust, we also support mental health and stronger communities."

data.title: Scientists discover never-before-seen part of human cells
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 科学家在人类细胞中发现了一种新的细胞器，称为“半融合体”（hemifusome）。这一结构是在使用冷冻电子断层扫描技术（cryo-ET）观察细胞时发现的，直径约100纳米，比线粒体还小。半融合体由两个通过双层脂质膜部分融合的囊泡组成，可能参与蛋白质分类、回收和丢弃。传统成像技术由于处理步骤苛刻，未能发现这一结构。研究人员认为，半融合体是细胞内的独立功能单元，而非暂时性结构，但其具体作用、生命周期和组成尚待进一步研究确认。这一发现揭示了细胞内一种新的潜在回收途径。

44434472.article_content:
The green and orange structures in this image are hemifusomes, newly discovered organelles that may represent a previously unrecognized pathway for recycling in human cells.
(Image credit: Courtesy UVA Health)
A new organelle has been discovered in human cells — and scientists call it a "hemifusome."
Like the full-size organs in our bodies, the organelles within cells are specialized structures that carry out specific functions. While observing filaments that maintain the shape of cells,
Seham Ebrahim
, an assistant professor at the University of Virginia, and her team noticed a new structure that was consistently appearing in the 3D images they were making.
What at first seemed like an artifact in the images turned out to be a new organelle that may be involved in sorting, recycling and discarding proteins within human cells. Ebrahim likened the hemifusome's shape to that of a snowman wearing a scarf; picture a small head attached to a larger body, with a thin border separating the two ends.

The organelle is around 100 nanometers in diameter, less than half the size of even a small mitochondrion, the famous powerhouse of the cell.
The scientists were able to observe the hemifusomes because they used a method called cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) to generate their images. This technique involved rapidly freezing cells from four lab-raised cell lines to preserve as much of their structures as possible, making it possible to create clear, 3D images.
"It's like a snapshot in time without any kind of chemical or any kind of stain," Ebrahim told Live Science. Using this imaging technique, they could look inside cells in a "very native state," as if they were glass balls, she said.

In their paper, published in the journal
Nature Communications
in May, the researchers wrote that the harsh processing steps that other imaging techniques subject cells to likely prevented hemifusomes from being observed earlier. In addition, with other techniques that use imaging to study the traffic unfolding in a living cell, the organelle was probably too small to be seen, appearing at most as a blur, Ebrahim added.
Ebrahim and her colleagues were looking at a configuration of vesicles they had never observed before. Vesicles are balloon-like structures used to transport things like proteins and hormones within and between cells. The new study revealed two vesicles fused together with a two-layer barrier of fat between them.
"Even from a biophysics perspective, it's a breakthrough," Ebrahim said, "because biophysically, people have always predicted, or theorized, that vesicles can exist in this hemifused state … but this was the first time that it has actually been seen in a living cell." This observation inspired the name hemifusome, since hemifusion refers to the partial merger of two bilayers.
This cryo-electron tomography image (left) and two corresponding schematics (center and right) highlight the distinctive structure of a hemifusome, where two vesicle membranes connect through a hemifusion diaphragm.
(Image credit: Courtesy UVA Health)
Ebrahim argues that hemifusomes can be classified as organelles because they are self-contained functional units within a cell, as opposed to "fleeting" structures that temporarily appear as membranes form and split. In the paper, she wrote that it's unlikely hemifusomes are artifacts of cryo-ET.
Ebrahim's findings "suggest that the hemifusomes they visualize are genuine cellular intermediates, not freezing-induced distortions," said
Yi-Wei Chang
, an assistant professor of biochemistry and biophysics at the University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine who was not involved in the work.
Once the role and function of hemifusomes have been confirmed through further studies, they may be recognized as their own class of intermediate structures that fulfill part of fusion processes in mammalian cells, Chang told Live Science in an email.

44434472.article_summary: 科学家在人类细胞中发现了一种新的细胞器，称为“半融合体”（hemifusome）。这一结构是在使用冷冻电子断层扫描技术（cryo-ET）观察细胞时发现的，直径约100纳米，比线粒体还小。半融合体由两个通过双层脂质膜部分融合的囊泡组成，可能参与蛋白质分类、回收和丢弃。传统成像技术由于处理步骤苛刻，未能发现这一结构。研究人员认为，半融合体是细胞内的独立功能单元，而非暂时性结构，但其具体作用、生命周期和组成尚待进一步研究确认。这一发现揭示了细胞内一种新的潜在回收途径。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的延迟影响、使用场景比较、模型性能对比及优化

不同观点：
• [pseudosavant] 关注该代理对请求的延迟影响，尤其是LLM对延迟的敏感性。虽然LLM对令牌生成时间较长，但仍关心代理引入的额外延迟。

• [jgant13] 询问该技术与OpenRouter的使用场景区分，尤其是何时选择该技术而非其他解决方案，如OpenRouter。

• [_nh_] 提出了与RouteLLM的比较，关心该技术与RouteLLM的优劣对比。

• [tmaly] 对模型的量化和性能表现感兴趣，询问是否可以在量化的同时保持良好的结果。

• [jedisct1] 分享了实际使用中的体验，指出该模型在编码任务难度评级中表现不如Qwen2.5-Coder-7B，并提到模型大小（1.5B对比7B）可能的影响。

补充讨论：
• [sparacha] 作为该论文的合著者，表示愿意回答有关其方法的任何问题，显示出对技术细节的开放讨论态度。

争议焦点：
• 不同模型之间的性能对比是讨论中的一个争议点，尤其是[jedisct1]提出的该模型与Qwen2.5-Coder-7B在实际应用中的表现差异。模型大小对性能的影响也是一个被提到的因素。

• 关于是否可以通过量化来优化模型性能，[tmaly]的提问暗示了对模型效率提升的潜在需求和可能性，但其实现可行性和效果尚待确认。

data.title: Figma Files Registration Statement for Proposed Initial Public Offering
data.author: kualto
data.article_summary: Figma于2025年7月1日宣布，已向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交Form S-1注册声明，计划进行首次公开募股（IPO），发行A类普通股，并在纽约证券交易所上市，股票代码为“FIG”。目前，具体发行股数和价格区间尚未确定，发行将取决于市场条件。摩根士丹利、高盛、Allen & Company LLC和J.P. Morgan等将担任此次发行的主承销商。此前，Figma已于4月秘密提交了S-1草案。此次IPO尚需SEC批准，才能正式生效。Figma是一个帮助团队协作设计数字产品的平台，成立于2012年，现已发展为一个集成了AI功能的平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Figma的IPO及其背后的技术、商业和用户影响

不同观点：
• crossroadsguy认为，IPO通常标志着公司增长的顶峰，公众（散户投资者）可能成为最后的接盘者，难以在长期内获利。
• btown对Figma的技术成就和商业成功表示钦佩，强调其工程设计和产品优化是其成功的关键，并对团队的创新精神表示赞赏。

• StableAlkyne认为，公司上市通常对用户不利，尽管目前Figma是一个优秀的设计工具，但上市后可能会因股东压力而降低用户体验。

• 用户对IPO后公司策略变化的担忧，尤其是对产品方向和用户体验的影响。
• 对Figma治理结构中CEO集中投票权的关注，可能影响公司未来的决策和透明度。

data.title: Code⇄GUI bidirectional editing via LSP
data.author: jamesbvaughan
data.article_summary: 作者James B. Vaughan开发了一个概念验证系统，实现了现代代码编辑器与图形用户界面（GUI）之间的实时双向编辑。该系统通过语言服务器协议（LSP）实现，允许用户在首选代码编辑器（如Emacs）中编辑代码，同时自动更新GUI，反之亦然。这一概念在代码CAD系统中尤为实用。尽管双向编辑并非新概念，但与常用文本编辑器的实时双向编辑则是创新之处。现有的工具如Fusion 360和OpenSCAD仅部分实现此功能。作者希望这一演示能激发更多对LSP服务器创意应用的探索，并期待看到更多关于codeCAD的开发进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过双向编辑实现语义编辑、GUI操作及其实时反馈的工具和方法

不同观点：
• FloatArtifact认为双向编辑对于无障碍软件至关重要，尤其是在语音控制代码编辑和获取GUI元素方面，具有很高的实用价值。
• jasonjmcghee分享了自己在实时编码方面的实验，例如通过LSP实现实时更新运行程序，以及通过VS Code扩展实现滑块和颜色选择器等交互功能，表达了对这种技术的浓厚兴趣和探索精神。
• necovek指出使用LSP进行图形工作的参数化非常有用，并提到FreeCAD与Python绑定的经验，认为目前工具在编码与GUI之间切换的体验还不够流畅。
• mikewarot将当前技术与1990年代的Borland Delphi进行比较，强调了Pascal语言与GUI工具包的良好匹配性，同时也指出了C++等语言在GUI设计中的复杂性和局限性，期待LLMs能提高生产力。
• harrylepotter分享了在vscode中使用webviews进行类似操作的经验，指出在语言服务器与UI组件之间映射诊断信息的复杂性，并表示希望分享更详细的实现。
• rao-v讨论了CAD软件中的文件格式问题，指出目前缺乏能够捕捉设计概念的跨平台CAD文件格式，并提到OpenSCAD和STEP格式的局限性。
• williamcotton介绍了自己的项目，实现了GUI与shell管道的双向映射，并提供了截图和GIF说明。
• kennykartman提到fornjot这个CAD工具可能对相关需求有帮助，并对项目表示赞赏。
• ogoffart介绍了Slint GUI工具包及其LSP服务器，提供了在线演示，展示了通过LSP实现的实时预览和编辑功能。
• taeric回忆了自己对类似技术的兴奋，提到Minecraft的实时编码 session，表达了对这种技术的持续兴趣但尚未取得实质进展。
• junon表示即将开始类似的项目，开发以代码为核心的PCB编辑工具，认为当前讨论的技术是非常有价值的参考。
• rtcode_io分享了双向同步演示，特别是PDF方面的应用，展示了整个双向同步的实现。
• WillAdams提到曾建议在OpenPythonSCAD中实现类似的交互性，但担心细节问题会导致UI变得杂乱无章。
• pshc表达了对多模式协作编辑器的梦想，并鼓励继续努力。
• SwiftyBug对项目表示赞赏，并希望有人能在此基础上创建iOS应用的Interface Builder，以改善Xcode的糟糕体验。

补充讨论：
1. 讨论中多次提到LSP在双向编辑和实时反馈中的核心作用，以及其在不同领域（如代码编辑、GUI操作、CAD设计等）的广泛应用潜力。
2. 争议焦点在于当前工具在编码与GUI操作之间的切换体验不够流畅，以及文件格式和语言支持的局限性。
3. 多个参与者分享了个人项目和实验，展示了双向编辑和实时反馈技术的实际应用和可能性。
4. 讨论还涉及了历史技术（如Borland Delphi）与现代技术的比较，以及LLMs在提高生产力方面的潜力。

Code⇄GUI bidirectional editing via LSP
Code⇄GUI bidirectional editing via LSP
Published:
2025-07-01T00:00:00Z
jamesbvaughan
https://jamesbvaughan.com/
July 1, 2025
I built a small proof-of-concept for a system that enables real-time
bidirectional editing between any modern code editor and a GUI, enabled by an
LSP
1
server.
Code-based CAD
I like working on small projects at home that benefit from CAD. I’m also a
programmer with a personal development environment that I’ve spent years making
as cozy as possible. Naturally I’ve been interested in finding code-based CAD
system to use for my projects that allows me to use that cozy development
environment.
I read
a recent update from Kevin Lynagh about his ongoing work on
codeCAD
,
and this part on bidirectional editing stood out to me (emphasis mine):
For example: One idea I’m exploring is “bidirectional editing”, so geometry can
be manipulated using either:
a purpose-built graphical UI, or
the textual codeCAD language
If you graphically drag a point around, the coordinates in the source code
should automatically update.
If you edit the source code, the graphical UI should automatically update.
A simple way to test this idea is to throw a
<textarea>
in the UI that
displays the corresponding source code.
But to me, that feels terrible because I never want to be coding in some janky,
in-browser
<textarea>
— I want to be working with source code in Emacs, with
all of my familiar key bindings, color schemes, autocomplete, and decades of
cozy practice.
That’s the core appeal of a textual programming language.
But doing this properly is an absolute boatload of work:
How does the system rewrite source code? Is it mediated by files on disk with
reload on save? How do the editor and UI stay in sync and avoid clobbering
each other’s unsaved changes?
Maybe we need an LSP server?
The language interpreter needs to preserve comments and flow them through,
even when the UI makes edits to the code.
What about whitespace / pretty-printing?
How much of this needs to be built to evaluate whether bidirectional editing
“fits nicely in the hand”?
In particular:
Maybe we need an LSP server?
I’ve been a happy user of LSP servers since they became commonplace in Neovim
setups
2
, but I have almost no experience with language server internals.
I had certainly never considered that they could facilitate bidirectional
editing with a GUI.
A proof-of-concept
That line from Kevin’s post was a proper nerd-snipe because a few hours later I
had built this proof-of-concept:
What you’re seeing here is a text editor next to a GUI, and data live-updating
both ways between them, made possible by a small server that uses LSP to
communicate with the text editor and WebSockets to communicate with a web app.
I’ve shared more technical details and the code for this demo
here on
GitHub
.
Why this excites me
Bidirectional editing isn’t new.
What’s new, as far as I’m aware, is real-time bidirectional editing
that works
with your favorite text editor.
I’ve tried out a handful of code-based CAD systems, but so far I haven’t found
any that achieve more than two out of these three features:
Real-time-ish updates in the GUI from changes made in the code
Real-time-ish updates in the code from changes made in the GUI
Works well with my preferred code editor
Fusion 360
has
decent bidirectional editing for parameters, but it’s not fully code-based and
it certainly doesn’t let me use my own editor.
OpenSCAD
doesn’t require the use of its own text
editor, and it’s possible to trigger reloads in the GUI via file watching
when you save source files in external editors, but it only goes one way.
Zoo
has some bidirectional editing, but only
with its built-in editor.
Arcol
, the tool that I help build at my day job
3
, is
innovating in CAD interface design in some exciting ways, but we’re building for
architects, not programmers.
This is just a toy demo, but it’s enough to excite me about the possibility of a
system that achieves
all three
of those points!
What’s next
I don’t plan to develop this demo further, at least not anytime soon, but I hope
it inspires people to find more creative uses (abuses?) of LSP servers.
One of the best code-CAD environments I’ve worked in is OpenSCAD + Neovim with
the
OpenSCAD LSP server
, only using
the OpenSCAD GUI for the viewer, not the built-in text editor.
OpenSCAD is fundamentally not built for GUI editing, but since it’s open source
and has a nice language server already, it could be a good place to develop a
more interesting demo of this concept.
Like Kevin’s post said, doing this properly will be a boatload of work.
Handling conflict resolution, incremental edits, and the more complex general
LSP server internals are all serious tasks, let alone creating a whole new
language for CAD.
I’m looking forward to seeing what Kevin comes up with for codeCAD!
LSP
is the
Language Server Protocol
.
It’s used by language servers to provide features like diagnostics, code
actions, go-to-definit
44435716.article_summary: 作者James B. Vaughan开发了一个概念验证系统，实现了现代代码编辑器与图形用户界面（GUI）之间的实时双向编辑。该系统通过语言服务器协议（LSP）实现，允许用户在首选代码编辑器（如Emacs）中编辑代码，同时自动更新GUI，反之亦然。这一概念在代码CAD系统中尤为实用。尽管双向编辑并非新概念，但与常用文本编辑器的实时双向编辑则是创新之处。现有的工具如Fusion 360和OpenSCAD仅部分实现此功能。作者希望这一演示能激发更多对LSP服务器创意应用的探索，并期待看到更多关于codeCAD的开发进展。

data.title: The Hidden Engineering of Liquid Dampers in Skyscrapers
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了高层建筑设计的新趋势——“铅笔塔”，这些建筑虽然不一定比过去的建筑高，但更加细长，通常高度与宽度的比例超过10:1。文章强调，设计这些细长建筑时，除了强度，还需要考虑其在风中晃动的问题，这被称为“可服务性极限状态”。为了减少晃动，工程师通常采用增加建筑刚度或改善空气动力学性能的方法，但这些方法可能会减少可用空间。因此，许多工程师使用调谐液体柱阻尼器（TLCD）来限制振动，这种装置通过水的运动来消耗能量，比复杂的机械阻尼器更简单且经济。文章通过自制模型演示了TLCD的工作原理，展示了其在减少建筑晃动方面的效果。

主要讨论点：建筑中的阻尼器，特别是液体阻尼器的功能、设计及其附加用途

不同观点：

• [ggm] 对非液体阻尼器（如台北101的调谐质量阻尼器）表示赞赏，认为其设计美学有吸引力，并质疑液体阻尼器是否能成为旅游景点。

• [Havoc] 对视频中的实际演示表示赞赏，认为尽管演示不一定100%成功，但比单纯讲解和使用一些半相关的动画要好。

• [chiph] 关注阻尼器中流体粘度对效果的影响，推测流体类型（如矿物油而非水）可能用于减少维护成本，特别是防止藻类生长。

补充讨论：
• 阻尼器的功能性：阻尼器在建筑中的主要作用是提高舒适性和保护建筑材料，还是对结构稳定性有更直接的贡献，成为讨论中的一个焦点。
• 阻尼器的设计美学：有评论提到阻尼器的设计不仅要考虑功能，还可以考虑其作为旅游景点的潜力，特别是与非液体阻尼器进行比较时。
• 流体选择与维护：有讨论提到阻尼器中使用的流体类型及其对维护成本的影响，特别是如何防止藻类生长等问题。

44437539.article_content:
[Note that this article is a transcript of the video embedded above.]
There’s a new trend in high-rise building design. Maybe you’ve seen this in your city. The best lots are all taken, so developers are stretching the limits to make use of space that isn’t always ideal for skyscrapers. They’re not necessarily taller than buildings of the past, but they are a lot more slender. “Pencil tower” is the term generally used to describe buildings that have a slenderness ratio of more than around 10 to 1, height to width. A lot of popular discussion around skyscrapers is about how tall we can build them. Eventually, you can get so tall that there are no materials strong enough to support the weight. But, pencil towers are the perfect case study in why strength isn’t the only design criterion used in structural engineering.
Of course, we don’t want our buildings to fall down, but there’s other stuff we don’t want them to do, too, including flex and sway in the wind. In engineering, this concept is called the serviceability limit state, and it’s an entirely separate consideration from strength. Even if moderate loads don’t cause a structure to fail, the movement they cause can lead to windows breaking, tiles cracking, accelerated fatigue of the structure, and, of course, people on the top floors losing their lunch from disorientation and discomfort. So, limiting wind-induced motions is a major part of high-rise design and, in fact, can be such a driving factor in the engineering of the building that strength is a secondary consideration.
Making a building stiffer is the obvious solution. But adding stiffness requires larger columns and beams, and those subtract valuable space within the building itself. Another option is to augment a building’s aerodynamic performance, reducing the loads that winds impose. But that too can compromise the expensive floorspace within. So many engineers are relying on another creative way to limit the vibrations of tall buildings. And of course, I built a model in the garage to show you how this works. I’m Grady, and this is Practical Engineering.
One of the very first topics I ever covered on this channel was tuned mass dampers. These are mechanisms that use a large, solid mass to counteract motion in all kinds of structures, dissipating the energy through friction or hydraulics, like the shock absorbers in vehicles. Probably the most famous of these is in the Taipei 101 building. At the top of the tower is a massive steel pendulum, and instead of hiding it away in a mechanical floor, they opened it to visitors, even giving the damper its own mascot. But, mass dampers have a major limitation because of those mechanical parts. The complex springs, dampers, and bearings need regular maintenance, and they are custom-built. That gets pretty expensive. So, what if we could simplify the device?
This is my garage-built high-rise. It’s not going to hold many conference room meetings, but it does do a good job swaying from side to side, just like an actual skyscraper. And I built a little tank to go on top here. The technical name for this tank is a tuned liquid column damper, and I can show you how it works. Let’s try it with no water first. Using my digitally calibrated finger, I push the tower over by a prescribed distance, and you can see this would not be a very fun ride. There is some natural damping, but the oscillation goes on for quite a while before the motion stops. Now, let’s put some water in the tank. With the power of movie magic, I can put these side by side so you can really get a sense of the difference.
By the way, nearly all of the parts for this demonstration were provided by my friends at Send-Cut-Send. I don’t have a milling machine or laser cutter, so this is a really nice option for getting customized parts made from basically any material - aluminum, steel, acrylic - that are ready to assemble.
Instead of complex mechanical devices, liquid column dampers dissipate energy through the movement of water. The liquid in the tank is both the mass and the damper. This works like a pendulum where the fluid oscillates between two columns. Normally, there’s an orifice between the two columns that creates the damping through friction loss as water flows from one side to the other. To make this demo a little simpler, I just put lids on the columns with small holes. I actually bought a fancy air valve to make this adjustable, but it didn’t allow quite enough airflow. So instead, I simplified with a piece of tape. Very technical. Energy transferred to the water through the building is dissipated by the friction of the air as it moves in and out of the columns. And you can even hear this as it happens.
Any supplemental damping system starts with a design criterion. This varies around the world, but in the US, this is probability-based. We generally require that peak accelerations with a 1-in-10 chance of being exceeded in a given year be limited to 15-18 milli-gs in residential build

data.title: Show HN: Core – open source memory graph for LLMs – shareable, user owned
data.author: Manik_agg
data.article_summary:
C.O.R.E（Contextual Observation & Recall Engine）是一个为大型语言模型（LLM）提供的个人记忆层，用户拥有完全控制权，可本地运行或使用托管版本，并与其他工具（如Cursor、Claude）连接以共享上下文。其核心功能包括：

1. 提供私密的个人记忆图谱，数据本地存储，跨应用访问。
2. 帮助AI助手（如SOL）获取用户上下文，提供个性化响应。
3. 动态知识图谱，记录事实的全历史，支持透明追溯。
4. 支持实时审计和变更追踪，例如价格变更或项目进展。

用户可通过Docker本地部署或使用C.O.R.E Cloud在线构建记忆图，并通过API与Cursor等工具集成。当前正改进对Llama模型的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）中的记忆系统设计及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [lukev] 认为在LLM中保持紧密、受限的上下文对获得正确结果很重要，但也指出让模型访问相关信息的同时排除不相关或混淆因素是一个需要调和的张力。他提出如何确保模型既能获得必要信息，又能避免无关信息的干扰。

• [MarkMarine] 提出人类记忆的工作方式，分为直接获取事实和通过“感觉”触发检索过程。他认为当前LLM缺乏的是第二种系统，即在执行任务时建立工作集并触发检索的能力，而不是仅仅依赖训练中获得的知识。

• [adamkochanowicz] 强调C.O.R.E系统的独特性，它是一个动态、活生生的时间知识图谱，每个事实都有完整的历史记录，提供透明性，可以追溯来源、查看变化和探索系统“相信”某事的原因。

• [smcleod] 质疑该系统是否真正本地化，并指出其依赖单一的SaaS LLM提供商，认为这可能限制了系统的独立性和灵活性。

• [funnym0nk3y] 对简单文本文件与MCP（可能是某种控制程序）的可访问性相比，看不到该系统的优势，要求进一步说明。

• [_joel] 对该系统与简单的计划文件（plan.md）的区别感到好奇，希望了解其独特价值。

• [ianbicking] 自己正在构建记忆系统，对使用知识图谱/三元组表示法提出质疑，认为简单的平面陈述似乎足够且更贴近源材料。他讨论了三元组的稳定性和实用性，以及如何有效地表示和更新记忆，提出了对结构化和扁平化数据库表示法的思考。

• [khaledh] 回顾了“语义网”的历史，指出构建和维护知识图谱需要大量知识工程工作和工具，认为当前LLM需要手动提供正确上下文以弥补记忆不足的问题，呼应了历史上的技术挑战。

• [mt_] 提出了开放源项目没有对其CLAUDE.md进行版本控制的问题，质疑其管理实践。

• [sutterbomb] 对Graphiti from Zep与讨论中的系统进行比较，希望了解两者的优劣。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于使用复杂的知识图谱（如C.O.R.E）是否比简单的文本档案或平面数据库更有优势。一些评论者质疑三元组表示法的必要性和稳定性，而另一些则强调其动态透明性和追踪能力。

• 讨论还涉及到如何在LLM中实现类似人类的记忆检索过程，特别是如何在执行任务时触发相关信息的检索，而不是单纯依赖训练数据。

• 另外，系统的依赖性和本地化问题也被提出，质疑其对单一SaaS提供商的依赖以及是否真正实现了本地化。

C.O.R.E.
Contextual Observation & Recall Engine
C.O.R.E is a shareable memory for LLMs which is private, portable and 100% owned by the user. You can either run it locally or use our hosted version and then connect with other tools like Cursor, Claude to share your context at multiple places.
C.O.R.E is built for two reasons:
To give you complete ownership of your memory, stored locally and accessible across any app needing LLM context.
To help SOL (your AI assistant) access your context, facts, and preferences for more relevant and personalized responses.
Note:
We are actively working on improving support for Llama models. At the moment, C.O.R.E does not provide optimal results with Llama-based models, but we are making progress to ensure better compatibility and output in the near future.
Demo Video
Check C.O.R.E Demo
How is C.O.R.E different from other Memory Providers?
Unlike most memory systems—which act like basic sticky notes, only showing what’s true right now. C.O.R.E is built as a dynamic, living temporal knowledge graph:
Every fact is a first-class “Statement” with full history, not just a static edge between entities.
Each statement includes what was said, who said it, when it happened, and why it matters.
You get full transparency: you can always trace the source, see what changed, and explore why the system “believes” something.
Use Case Example: Real Change Auditing
Imagine you ask SOL: "What changed in our pricing since Q1?"
With C.O.R.E, you see exactly what prices changed, who approved them, the context (meeting, email, document), and when each update happened—enabling true compliance, auditability, and insight across products, teams, and time.
Or ask: “What does Mike know about Project Phoenix?” and get a timeline of meetings, decisions, and facts Mike was involved in, with full traceability to those specific events.

44435500.article_summary:
C.O.R.E（Contextual Observation & Recall Engine）是一个为大型语言模型（LLM）提供的个人记忆层，用户拥有完全控制权，可本地运行或使用托管版本，并与其他工具（如Cursor、Claude）连接以共享上下文。其核心功能包括：

1. 提供私密的个人记忆图谱，数据本地存储，跨应用访问。
2. 帮助AI助手（如SOL）获取用户上下文，提供个性化响应。
3. 动态知识图谱，记录事实的全历史，支持透明追溯。
4. 支持实时审计和变更追踪，例如价格变更或项目进展。

用户可通过Docker本地部署或使用C.O.R.E Cloud在线构建记忆图，并通过API与Cursor等工具集成。当前正改进对Llama模型的支持。
44435500.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）中的记忆系统设计及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [lukev] 认为在LLM中保持紧密、受限的上下文对获得正确结果很重要，但也指出让模型访问相关信息的同时排除不相关或混淆因素是一个需要调和的张力。他提出如何确保模型既能获得必要信息，又能避免无关信息的干扰。

• [MarkMarine] 提出人类记忆的工作方式，分为直接获取事实和通过“感觉”触发检索过程。他认为当前LLM缺乏的是第二种系统，即在执行任务时建立工作集并触发检索的能力，而不是仅仅依赖训练中获得的知识。

• [adamkochanowicz] 强调C.O.R.E系统的独特性，它是一个动态、活生生的时间知识图谱，每个事实都有完整的历史记录，提供透明性，可以追溯来源、查看变化和探索系统“相信”某事的原因。

• [smcleod] 质疑该系统是否真正本地化，并指出其依赖单一的SaaS LLM提供商，认为这可能限制了系统的独立性和灵活性。

• [funnym0nk3y] 对简单文本文件与MCP（可能是某种控制程序）的可访问性相比，看不到该系统的优势，要求进一步说明。

• [_joel] 对该系统与简单的计划文件（plan.md）的区别感到好奇，希望了解其独特价值。

• [ianbicking] 自己正在构建记忆系统，对使用知识图谱/三元组表示法提出质疑，认为简单的平面陈述似乎足够且更贴近源材料。他讨论了三元组的稳定性和实用性，以及如何有效地表示和更新记忆，提出了对结构化和扁平化数据库表示法的思考。

• [khaledh] 回顾了“语义网”的历史，指出构建和维护知识图谱需要大量知识工程工作和工具，认为当前LLM需要手动提供正确上下文以弥补记忆不足的问题，呼应了历史上的技术挑战。

• [mt_] 提出了开放源项目没有对其CLAUDE.md进行版本控制的问题，质疑其管理实践。

• [sutterbomb] 对Graphiti from Zep与讨论中的系统进行比较，希望了解两者的优劣。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于使用复杂的知识图谱（如C.O.R.E）是否比简单的文本档案或平面数据库更有优势。一些评论者质疑三元组表示法的必要性和稳定性，而另一些则强调其动态透明性和追踪能力。

• 讨论还涉及到如何在LLM中实现类似人类的记忆检索过程，特别是如何在执行任务时触发相关信息的检索，而不是单纯依赖训练数据。

• 另外，系统的依赖性和本地化问题也被提出，质疑其对单一SaaS提供商的依赖以及是否真正实现了本地化。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JS1K竞赛的重启及其相关技术问题和回忆

不同观点：
• **对使用ChatGPT的批评**：[averageRoyalty] 认为使用ChatGPT生成提交内容让人对项目的原创性和质量产生怀疑，从而减少了他们关注该项目的可能性。

• **对JS1K重启的怀旧和支持**：[binarymax] 和 [mr_sturd] 对JS1K的回归表示欢迎和怀念，回忆起早期参与竞赛的经历，并分享了首届JS1K的demo链接。[binarymax] 特别提到这一竞赛让JS demoscene得以延续。

• **现代浏览器潜力的讨论**：[xnx] 提到，现代浏览器内置的功能让在1K大小内实现 impressive 效果成为可能，并引用了140字符的JavaScript创意平台 Dwitter 作为例子，暗示技术的进步让竞赛更加有趣。

• **关于竞赛规则和框架使用的争议**：[zamadatix] 对竞赛中使用shims（垫片）和框架的问题提出了看法，认为竞赛应强调纯粹的代码，不应依赖框架。他指出，虽然有些获奖作品使用了shims，但其他未使用shims的作品可能更值得认可，并建议根据所用方法而非起始框架来评判作品。

• **对竞赛规则的疑问**：[econ] 对竞赛是否允许使用DOM或必须使用canvas提出了疑问，显示出对竞赛具体规则的不确定。

补充讨论：
• **技术问题**：[mg794613] 提到网站可能因为访问量过大导致示例无法加载，暗示竞赛重启后可能面临的技术问题。

• **创意灵感的分享**：[leptons] 分享了Dwitter上的热门作品链接，为寻找灵感的人提供了资源。

• **对JavaScript的简单赞美**：[revskill] 简短地表达了对JavaScript的喜爱，强调了JS的趣味性。

争议焦点：竞赛中使用框架和shims的合理性，以及是否应根据所用方法而非框架来评判作品。这引发了对竞赛公平性和规则透明度的讨论。

data.title: The Roman Roads Research Association
data.author: bjourne
data.article_summary: 罗马道路研究协会（RRRA）致力于推进对罗马道路网络的研究，特别是在不列颠群岛地区。协会继承了Ivan D. Margary的研究，利用现代技术如LiDAR来揭示隐藏的古道。协会出版学术期刊《Itinera》，接受关于罗马道路及交通基础设施的研究投稿，第六卷将于2025年11月15日截稿。协会还举办系列在线讲座，涵盖罗马道路及相关考古发现。协会正开发新网站，以提升功能和现代感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国道路与古罗马道路的关系，以及现代和古代道路建设的对比

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为许多英国现代道路，如A68和A1部分路段以及Watling Street，是沿着或靠近罗马时代道路修建的。他提出，罗马人选择直线建造道路更多是出于实际 genius（实用天才）而非诅咒，因为这在当时的测量工具条件下是可行的，且易于传达给工人和劳力。他还用现代澳大利亚丛林道路中存在不明原因的弯曲为例，戏谑地推测可能是修路工人感到无聊所致。

• [mkarliner] 对[ggm]的观点表示赞同和共鸣，提到自己住在距离Watling Street几百米的地方（Cricklewood Broadway），表明亲身体验了这些历史道路的存在和影响。

• [car] 提供了一个额外的信息来源，指出通过Lidar技术也识别出了史前田地，并附上一个关于凯尔特田地的网站链接，将讨论扩展到古罗马道路之外的史前遗迹。

• [nvader] 对讨论持怀疑态度，质疑这些讨论是否仅属于Roads Research Association（道路研究协会）的范畴，暗示这可能是一个专门领域的兴趣话题，而非大众关注点。

• [hjrnunes] 提供了另一个资源，推荐了一个名为Isaac Moreno的西班牙YouTube频道，认为对罗马道路和罗马工程感兴趣的人值得一看，将讨论引向具体的媒体资源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体例子和资源链接，如Watling Street的现代位置、Lidar技术识别史前田地的网站以及YouTube频道，提供了进一步探索的途径。
• 争议的焦点可能在于这些道路建设历史和技术的讨论是否仅限于特定领域的研究，以及现代道路设计中存在的不规则性是否真的如[ggm]所戏称的是由于工人主观因素。

总的来说，讨论围绕古代罗马道路对现代道路的影响，以及如何利用现代技术识别和研究古代遗迹展开，同时提供了具体的实例和资源供进一步探索。

The Roman Roads Research Association was formed to advance knowledge of the Roman road network and promote the study of Roman roads and Roman heritage throughout the British Isles. Our work is inspired by Ivan D. Margary whose âRoman Roads in Britain â (1955) remains the most comprehensive gazetteer ever compiled.
We continue Margaryâs work by researching Roman roads using modern technology such as LiDAR, which uses lasers fired from an aircraft to create an incredibly accurate model of the earthâs surface beneath any vegetation, revealing surviving archaeology otherwise not visible. The example below is a Roman road in Lincolnshire, just east of Grantham, where until recently it was assumed that the A52 followed the course of a Roman road, which it almost certainly doesnât. Instead, a different road leads from the same junction on Ermine Street, apparently serving an entirely local function.

The fifth volume of the Roman Roads Research Associationâs own peer reviewed journal,
Itinera
, will be released in digital form to our members in June 2025, with printed versions available to
purchase
for delivery in late May. We are now accepting submissions for Volume 6.
Itinera
is the only journal in the world dedicated to publishing research, fieldwork, and new discoveries that relate to Roman roads or Roman transport infrastructure more broadly, both in Britannia and the rest of the Roman Empire.
We welcome papers which contribute to a better understanding of the road network and its place within the wider context of Roman studies, whether in the UK or internationally.
Itinera includes reports of excavations, new discoveries from lidar, aerial photography, and geophysics, designation of 'new' routes through an expanded Margary system, and a range of peer-
reviewed scholarly articles exploring the wider context of roads as related to military and civilian activity, forts, planning, surveying and all aspects of Roman life. Itinera 6 will include
Roman Roads in 2025
, providing an overview of all archaeological work involving Roman roads in Britain during the coming year. Full details, including Notes for Contibutors, can be found

data.author: karchaw
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了当前信息秩序的变革，传统机构如新闻、学术和教育等正在解体，而大型语言模型（LLMs）等新技术尚未形成稳定的新秩序。LLMs不同于传统的数据库或搜索引擎，它们更像是“意义机器”或“现实合成器”，通过吸收人类意义生成的深层模式来即兴创作。然而，这种即时生成信息的能力既令人陶醉又危险，因为它削弱了“核实”或“验证”信息的重要性。

LLMs还具有一种“环境意识形态”，即对现实的潜在假设，如“共识通常正确”或“每个问题都有答案”。这种意识形态虽不明显，却影响着它们提供的解决方案和视角。当我们依赖LLMs进行意义生成时，实际上是在吸收其隐含的世界观，可能忽视其潜在的偏见。

文章最后将信息景观比作一个需要导航的领域，传统机构提供了明确的路径，而社交媒体使其变得无序，LLMs虽看似完美的向导，但实际上更像是随机应变的“即兴演奏者”。

Slouching Towards Sensemaking
There’s a particular quality to the confusion of our current moment that reminds me of standing in Dolores Park at dusk, watching fog roll in from Twin Peaks while the Mission stays stubbornly sunny. We’re between weather systems, between worlds. The old information order – built on broadcast towers and printing presses, gatekeepers and institutions – is visibly dissolving. The new one hasn’t quite condensed into recognizable forms yet. We’re in the interregnum, and it’s both terrifying and thrilling.
The thing is, we’ve been here before. Sort of.
Every era has its dominant metaphor for how knowledge works. The Enlightenment gave us the mind as a blank slate, waiting to be written upon by experience. The industrial age reimagined thinking as a kind of factory, processing raw inputs into refined outputs. The computer age taught us to think of brains as information processors, running algorithms on data.
Now we have LLMs, and they’re scrambling all our metaphors. They’re not databases – they don’t store and retrieve information in any conventional sense. They’re not search engines – they don’t point you to existing content. They’re more like… meaning machines? Reality synthesizers? Semantic improvisers?
The closest analogy I can find comes from music. A jazz musician doesn’t memorize every possible melody. Instead, they internalize patterns, relationships, and structures that let them generate novel-but-coherent musical phrases in real time. LLMs do something similar with language and concepts. They’ve absorbed the deep patterns of human meaning-making and can riff on them endlessly.
But here’s the catch: a jazz musician knows when they’re improvising. We don’t always recognize when an LLM is making things up.
To understand where we’re headed, it helps to see what’s being taken apart. The 20th century bundled several functions into single institutions:
Fact-gathering and verification (journalism)
Analysis and interpretation (academia)
Narrative construction (media)
Cultural transmission (education)
Collective sensemaking (democratic deliberation)
These institutions were never perfect, but they provided structured processes for turning raw information into shared understanding. They had gatekeepers, methodologies, and accountability mechanisms. They moved slowly, but that slowness enabled certain kinds of rigor.
LLMs unbundle all of these functions and make them available on-demand, at arbitrary scale, with zero marginal cost. Want fact-checking? Analysis? A compelling narrative? Cultural context? It’s all there, instantaneously, tailored to your specific query.
This is intoxicating. It’s also dangerous. When you can generate plausible-sounding information about anything instantaneously, the very idea of “checking” or “verifying” starts to break down. The speed of generation outpaces the speed of verification by orders of magnitude.
Here’s something I’ve noticed: LLMs don’t just have biases (though they do). They have what I call an “ambient ideology” – a pervasive orientation toward reality that colors everything they produce. This isn’t explicitly political. It’s more like a set of unexamined assumptions about how the world works:
Consensus is usually correct
Complexity can be simplified without loss
All perspectives can be reconciled
Conflict is a communication problem
Every question has an answer
Uncertainty is temporary
These assumptions aren’t necessarily wrong, but they’re not neutral either. They shape how LLMs frame issues, what solutions they propose, what possibilities they can and can’t imagine. And because this ideology is ambient – built into the very structure of how these systems generate text – it’s incredibly hard to notice, much less resist.
When we outsource our sensemaking to these systems, we’re not just getting help processing information. We’re absorbing their implicit worldview, their way of constructing meaning. It’s like wearing tinted glasses so long you forget the world isn’t actually pink.
If information is a landscape, then understanding is about navigation – finding paths between ideas, mapping territories of knowledge, recognizing landmarks of truth. Traditional institutions created well-worn paths through this landscape. Textbooks, curricula, and canons were like marked trails – they told you which routes were safe, which vistas were worth seeing, which areas to avoid. These paths had ideological assumptions built in, sure, but at least those assumptions were relatively visible and contestable.
Social media turned the landscape into a trackless waste. Every point connects to every other point with no clear paths between them. You can teleport instantly from vaccine research to ancient aliens to your high school friend’s wedding photos. The topology is flat, directionless, disorienting.

data.title: Swearing as a Response to Pain: Assessing Effects of Novel Swear Words
data.author: sega_sai
data.article_summary: 这篇文章研究了咒骂作为对疼痛的反应是否能减轻痛感，特别关注情感激发和分心作为潜在机制。实验比较了传统咒骂词“fuck”和两个新造的类咒骂词“fouch”和“twizpipe”的效果。参与者（N=92）在进行冷压疼痛测试时重复说这些词。结果显示，传统咒骂词“fuck”显著提高了疼痛阈值和耐痛能力，且情感、幽默和分心评分增加。然而，新造词“fouch”和“twizpipe”尽管在情感和幽默评分上高于中性词，但对疼痛阈值或耐痛能力无影响。研究还发现分心并非关键机制，而情感激发值得进一步研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论中围绕咒骂词（swear words）的使用、效果及其在不同情境下的影响展开讨论，包括教育、情感表达、疼痛缓解等方面。

不同观点：
• **咒骂词在教育中的使用：**
  - [MattPalmer1086] 提到他的德语老师通过教授长咒骂词来使课程更生动，并通过幽默方式帮助学生记忆。
  - [dtgriscom] 分享了自己高中学习俄语时，记住了一些类似咒骂的发音，这成为学习中的趣事。

• **咒骂词对情绪和疼痛的影响：**
  - [techdmn] 分享了自己鼓励女儿在情绪激动时通过说咒骂词来释放压力，并认为这种方式有助于情感处理。
  - [somedude895] 持相反观点，认为过度使用咒骂词会使其失去力量，主张谨慎使用以保持其影响力。
  - [lxe] 引用了实验结果，指出某些咒骂词如“fuck”在缓解疼痛方面有实际效果，而其他自创的咒骂词则无此效果。

• **替代咒骂词的使用：**
  - [carpo] 尝试用“sugarplum fairies”替代咒骂词，虽然在某些情况下成功，但在极端疼痛时仍会混合使用咒骂词，引发了幽默效果。
  - [kulahan] 提出咒骂词可能具有某种特定的发音结构，使得它们在表达情绪时更具力量，并讨论了不同替代词的可能性。

• **咒骂词对表现的影响：**
  - [anoncow] 引用了科学研究，指出咒骂词不仅在疼痛缓解上有作用，还能在愉悦感、力量和表现提升方面产生影响。

• **个人经验和主观感受：**
  - [timewizard] 认为咒骂词会使情况变得更糟，主张用简单的表达如“ow!”或“that hurt!”来更快地度过疼痛时刻。
  - [goopypoop] 以幽默方式提到通过咒骂词来自我调节，并提及了设立咒骂罐（swear jar）的做法。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还提到了与流行文化的关联，如[1317]推荐的视频和[Finnucane]引用的幽默语句，增加了讨论的趣味性。
• 一些评论如[phantomathkg]将讨论与《Mythbusters》这样的实验性节目进行类比，强调了对咒骂词效果的实验性验证。

争议焦点：咒骂词的效果因人而异，一些人认为其在情绪处理和疼痛缓解上有积极作用，而另一些人则主张节制使用以避免其失去效力。

ORIGINAL RESEARCH article
Front. Psychol.
, 30 April 2020
Sec. Health Psychology
Volume 11 - 2020 |
https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2020.00723
Swearing as a Response to Pain: Assessing Hypoalgesic Effects of Novel “Swear” Words
Richard Stephens
1*
Olly Robertson
2,3
1
School of Psychology, Keele University, Keele, United Kingdom
2
School of Psychology, Keele University, Keele, United Kingdom
3
Department of Experimental Psychology, University of Oxford, Oxford, United Kingdom
Previous research showing that swearing alleviates pain is extended by addressing emotion arousal and distraction as possible mechanisms. We assessed the effects of a conventional swear word (“fuck”) and two new “swear” words identified as both emotion-arousing and distracting: “fouch” and “twizpipe.” A mixed sex group of participants (
N
= 92) completed a repeated measures experimental design augmented by mediation analysis. The independent variable was repeating one of four different words: “fuck” vs. “fouch” vs. “twizpipe” vs. a neutral word. The dependent variables were emotion rating, humor rating, distraction rating, cold pressor pain threshold, cold pressor pain tolerance, pain perception score, and change from resting heart rate. Mediation analyses were conducted for emotion, humor, and distraction ratings. For conventional swearing (“fuck”), confirmatory analyses found a 32% increase in pain threshold and a 33% increase in pain tolerance, accompanied by increased ratings for emotion, humor, and distraction, relative to the neutral word condition. The new “swear” words, “fouch” and “twizpipe,” were rated as more emotional and humorous than the neutral word but did not affect pain threshold or tolerance. Changes in heart rate and pain perception were absent. Our data replicate previous findings that repeating a swear word at a steady pace and volume benefits pain tolerance, extending this finding to pain threshold. Mediation analyses did not identify a pathway via which such effects manifest. Distraction appears to be of little importance but emotion arousal is worthy of future study.
Introduction
Swearing, defined as the use of taboo language conveying connotative information (
Jay and Janschewitz, 2008
), is a near-universal feature of language (
van Lancker and Cummings, 1999
). Research has shown that repeating a swear word can be an effective way of increasing tolerance for the physical pain of an ice water challenge (
Stephens et al., 2009
;
Stephens and Umland, 2011
;
Robertson et al., 2017
) and the social pain associated with ostracism (
Philipp and Lombardo, 2017
).
In explaining how swearing brings about these pain reducing effects, one theory posits that swearing brings about a stress-induced analgesia (
Stephens and Umland, 2011
;
Philipp and Lombardo, 2017
) via increased autonomic arousal. Consistent with this theory, several studies have shown that swearing provokes an autonomic response, assessed via increased heart rate (
Stephens et al., 2009
;
Stephens and Umland, 2011
) and increased skin conductance (
LaBar and Phelps, 1998
;
Jay et al., 2008
;
Bowers and Pleydell-Pearce, 2011
). It is the emotion-provoking aspect of swearing that is thought to underlie this increase in autonomic arousal (
Stephens and Allsop, 2012
).
It would be of theoretical interest to further assess the importance of emotional arousal as a means by which swearing brings about pain relief. A novel way to assess this would be to test whether a newly made-up “swear” word, chosen because it has potential to elicit an emotional response, produces similar pain reducing effects as swearing.
An alternative theory explaining how swearing brings about pain reducing effects is via attention modulation (
Wiech et al., 2008
). It is established within the framework of the descending pain inhibitory system that cognitive processes, including distracting attention away from a pain stimulus, can reduce perceived pain (
Edwards et al., 2009
). The precise mechanism appears to be a combination of inhibiting sensory and emotional brain regions, while at the same time acting in an excitatory capacity on the periaqueductal gray region of the brain where endogenous opioids such as endorphins are produced (
Sims-Williams et al., 2017
).
One property of swearing that may usefully distract one’s attention from pain is if the word is perceived as humorous or novel. That swearing can be perceived as funny has been shown by
Engelthaler and Hills (2018)
, who had 821 participants rate 5000 English words for humor. The word “fuck” was rated in the top 1% of funniest words. Similarly, swearing is perceived as a novel unit of language, evidenced by findings estimating that swear words make up less than 1% of all speech (
Jay, 2009
). Given that human attention appears biased toward detecting stimuli that occur less frequently over those occurring more frequently (
Horstmann and Herwig, 2016
), it would be of theoretical interest to further assess the importance of atte

data.title: The wanton destruction of a creative-tech era
data.author: gregsadetsky
data.article_summary: 这篇文章激烈批评了Fastly公司决定关闭Glitch.com的决定。Glitch是一个让人们创作、分享和灵感碰撞的网站，因其社区和创意环境受到喜爱。作者指责Fastly为了商业利益背弃了用户信任，制造了大量的404错误页面，并可能损害其在CDN市场的声誉。文章充满了讽刺和愤怒，表达了对Glitch关闭的深切失望和悲痛，并调侃地提出以表演和个人牺牲换取延长关闭时间的建议。最终，作者认为这种决定是无情的企业行为，忽视了用户的感受和社区的价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户与客户的区别以及免费产品商业模式的可持续性

不同观点：
• bruce511认为用户和客户是不同的，用户不直接支付账单，而客户（如风投公司）才是公司优化的对象。他指出，用户常期望产品免费，但这与产品的长期生存相矛盾。虽然付费不能保证产品一定存活，但不付费则几乎保证了产品无法长久维持。
• robotnikman对bruce511的观点表示感慨，认为当不坚持某些价值观时，创造价值变得容易，暗示对商业化的不满或失望。
• monster_truck指出，很多真诚的用户并不完全了解平台背后的复杂性，包括平台曾被滥用的问题，尽管团队已尽力阻止。

补充讨论：
• pvg提供了一个相关讨论的链接，引导读者查看另一个讨论线程以获取更多信息。
• chaosprint表达了对平台关闭的惋惜，回忆起曾在那里看到的优秀创意作品，并提到用户正迁移到其他平台如Netlify和Cloudflare。

争议焦点：
• 用户是否应视为客户以及免费产品模式的可持续性是讨论的主要争议点。bruce511强调用户与客户的区别及免费模式的局限性，而其他评论者则关注平台的价值和用户迁移问题。

44437015.article_content:
Fastly, you killed glitch.com and ruined your karma for 10,000 years. You have “
betrayed yourself for nothing
.”
Glitch was an idealistic place where people gathered and made sites, were inspired by other people’s sites and remixed them, and generally enjoyed themselves. Of course a site like that takes money to run, of course you need people to run it - it was specifically better because of the people that ran it. And I can only be very sympathetic to the fact that it cost money - that it only existed because of money - and maybe the reality of that site ever existing was a mirage. Maybe we never deserved a place that made creation easy, maybe a community of people who loved to work together and share should never have existed. Maybe it would have been better if we never cared! That would have been easier and cheaper too. I’m sorry anyone ever felt happy there.
But you gutless monsters bought it - you spent money on it. Why? Venture capital back-dealing? Friends of friends of friends of friends back-scratching? Someone somewhere had to cash out on
their
investment, so here’s a nice public company that will end up making good on everyone’s past rounds? I have no clue! Maybe someone at Fastly actually believed in Glitch for an honest nanosecond but then changed their minds. Which led to this extraordinary linkicide - yes, my beautiful Fastly babies, you just smothered the web with millions of 404s all pointing back to you. Will all future dead Glitch urls redirect to https://www.fastly.com/contact-sales ?
I hope that when every LLM starts answering questions like “what’s the best enterprise cdn” and “what’s the most reliable cdn” or “where should I host my cdn I am the president of pharma”, you show up as an alternative not worthy of trust. “Fastly has been shown to abandon millions of sites without a care in the world, telling users and customers that they have a month to get the most absolutely fucking furthest out of the way. You should not consider them for your Fortune 1000.”
No but truly, I’m sorry. 99.8% of the people involved - Fastly employees, fans, supporters, users - had nothing to do with this. This is malice that could only have come from an enterprise executive. A committee maybe? It would honestly feel better if this was some sort of firing by LLM. Did ChatGPT make you a slide deck called “this quarter’s misery” and grouped the killing of Glitch with other smart cost saving measures such as LED lightbulbs and single ply toilet paper? You guys rock. Saving money, creating shareholder value… It’s easy to create value when you don’t have values.
Could I buy a single 6.98 USD stock (actual current price, ouch I shouldn’t have looked at that Google Finance graph, I almost started feeling bad) and show up at a shareholder event? Could I performatively dance the pain of millions of sites dying? Would you watch? Would you cry - do you remember how?
Yes, in this beautiful messy world of wars, famine and raw milk detoxfluencers, the ending of an internet website host ranks as a LOW priority. It should not be on anyone’s radar. It is a reality that we should ignore. They’re just feelings, and feelings are not real. Life goes by. “
Ars longa, vita brevis
”, except if your Ars is hosted by Fastly. Then your Ars will be extra, extra brevis.
Fastly, my loves, have you considered shame?
xx
P.s. I am SO not blackmailing you, but if you extended the Glitch shutdown date by, like, two years, I will write a beautiful retraction, I will drink a gallon of raw milk and I will stream it all live for your sadistic pleasure. Consider it a deal. 🤝.

data.title: HN Slop: AI startup ideas generated from Hacker News
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了名为"HN Slop"的工具，它能够从当前Hacker News首页提取信息，自动生成新鲜的AI创业点子。文章描述了该工具的运行过程，包括从分析Hacker News帖子到生成创意想法的步骤，突出了其创新性和即时性。该工具旨在为创业者和创新者提供灵感，帮助他们发现基于最新技术趋势的潜在商业机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成创业点子的平台及其相关功能、潜力和局限

不同观点：
• **支持和兴趣**：
   - [jpl56]: 认为AI生成个性化创业点子是可行的，并表现出兴趣。
   - [BiraIgnacio]: 对平台表示感谢和赞赏。
   - [trevor-e]: 认为将科学研究转化为易懂内容的平台会很有价值，有助于解决研究人员的推广问题。

• **功能和扩展建议**：
   - [wanderingstan]: 建议增加选择年份的功能，以获取特定年代的创业点子。
   - [mittermayr]: 建议连接到一个域名注册平台，以便为生成的点子提供可用域名。
   - [amelius]: 提到一个生成专利的AI可能是一个下一步的发展方向。

• **幽默和创意反应**：
   - [ForgotMyUUID]: 分享了一个复杂且有趣的创业点子，结合了多种技术元素。
   - [redsparrow]: 提供了一个幽默且夸张的点子，结合了个性化脏话和建筑稳定技术。
   - [piotraleksander]: 惊讶于没有包含"vibe"这个词的点子。
   - [butz]: 分享了一个详细且有趣的点子，并以幽默方式表示不浪费微小的经济价值。

• **批评和反思**：
   - [amelius]: 将平台与Halfbakery.com对比，认为人类生成的点子更有趣。
   - [shannifin]: 认为一些点子过于模糊，只是常见短语的组合，但仍觉得有趣。
   - [tdiff]: 认为点子本身没有太大价值，提醒人们注意这一点。

补充讨论：
- 评论中提到的各种AI生成点子的质量和实用性引发了关于创意和人类参与价值的讨论。
- 评论还展示了用户对特定功能和扩展的兴趣，以及对AI生成内容的幽默和创意反应。
- 争议的焦点可能在于AI生成点子的实际价值和创新性，以及人类创意在其中的作用。

data.article_summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman回应Meta CEO马克·扎克伯格近期挖角行为，在给员工的备忘录中强调留在OpenAI是实现人工通用智能（AGI）的最佳选择，暗示公司正评估整个研究团队的薪酬。他批评Meta的招聘手段可能导致深层次文化问题，并表示尽管Meta挖走了一些优秀人才，但OpenAI的核心团队和文化依然强大。Altman还提到，OpenAI专注于AGI的使命使其与众不同，而其他公司仅将AI视为实现其他目标的工具。多名高管也在Slack上发言，称赞OpenAI文化的优越性。Altman表示将公平调整薪酬，以留住人才。

OpenAI CEO Sam
Altman is hitting back at Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s recent AI talent-poaching spree. In a full-throated response sent to OpenAI researchers Monday evening and obtained by WIRED, Altman made his pitch for why staying at OpenAI is the only answer for those looking to build artificial general intelligence, hinting that the company is evaluating compensation for the entire research organization.
He also dismissed Meta’s recruiting efforts, saying what the company is doing could lead to deep cultural problems down the road.
“We have gone from some nerds in the corner to the most interesting people in the tech industry (at least),” he wrote on Slack. “AI Twitter is toxic; Meta is acting in a way that feels somewhat distasteful; I assume things will get even crazier in the future. After I got fired and came back I said that was not the craziest thing that would happen in OpenAl history; certainly neither is this.”
The news comes on the heels of a major announcement from Zuckerberg. On Monday, the Meta CEO
sent a memo
to staff introducing the company’s new superintelligence team, which will be helmed by Alexandr Wang, formerly of Scale AI, and Nat Friedman, who previously led GitHub. The list of new hires also included a number of
people from OpenAI
, including Shengjia Zhao, Shuchao Bi, Jiahui Yu, and Hongyu Ren. OpenAI’s chief research officer, Mark Chen,
told staff
that it felt like “someone has broken into our home and stolen something.”
Altman struck a different tone about the departures in his note on Monday.
“Meta has gotten a few great people for sure, but on the whole, it is hard to overstate how much they didn't get their top people and had to go quite far down their list; they have been trying to recruit people for a super long time, and I've lost track of how many people from here they've tried to get to be their Chief Scientist,” he wrote. “I am proud of how mission-oriented our industry is as a whole; of course there will always be some mercenaries.”
He added that “Missionaries will beat mercenaries” and noted that OpenAI is assessing compensation for the entire research organization. “I believe there is much, much more upside to OpenAl stock than Meta stock,” he wrote. “But I think it's important that huge upside comes after huge success; what Meta is doing will, in my opinion, lead to very deep cultural problems. We will have more to share about this soon but it's very important to me we do it fairly and not just for people who Meta happened to target.”
Got a Tip?
Do you know anything about the AI talent war? We'd like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact the reporter securely on Signal at zoeschiffer.87.
Altman then made his pitch for people to remain at OpenAI. “I have never been more confident in our research roadmap,” he wrote. “We are making an unprecedented bet on compute, but I love that we are doing it and I'm confident we will make good use of it. Most importantly of all, I think we have the most special team and culture in the world. We have work to do to improve our culture for sure; we have been through insane hypergrowth. But we have the core right in a way that I don't think anyone else quite does, and I'm confident we can fix the problems.”
“And maybe more importantly than that, we actually care about building AGI in a good way,” he added. “Other companies care more about this as an instrumental goal to some other mission. But this is our top thing, and always will be. Long after Meta has moved on to their next flavor of the week, or defending their social moat, we will be here, day after day, year after year, figuring out how to do what we do better than anyone else. A lot of other efforts will rise and fall too.”
A number of high-ranking employees who’ve worked at Meta followed up in Slack with their own stories about why OpenAI’s culture is superior. “[T]hey constantly rotate their top focus,” wrote one. Another said: “Yes we’re quirky and weird, but that’s what makes this place a magical cradle of innovation,” wrote one. “OpenAI is weird in the most magical way. We contain multitudes.”

data.title: Exploring Trichromacy through Maxwell's Color Experiment (2023)
data.author: niwrad
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦对三色视觉理论（也称杨-亥姆霍兹理论）的贡献。该理论解释了人眼如何通过三种颜色（红、绿、蓝）感知大部分颜色。麦克斯韦设计了一种实验装置，利用镜子、棱镜和透镜，通过三个不同位置的狭缝让特定波长的光进入，从而控制颜色组合及其强度。通过调整狭缝位置和宽度，麦克斯韦能够生成不同的颜色，证明了人眼通过三种基本颜色感知色彩的能力。这一实验为现代色彩显示技术奠定了基础。

44408484.article_content:
Exploring Trichromacy through Maxwell's Color Experiment
by
Koh Terai
with the guidance of
Professor Brian Wandell
for
Psych 221: Image Systems Engineering
at Stanford University
Last Updated:
19:30 Saturday, December 30, 2023 (PST)
We can create most of the colors we see daily using
just three colors
. For example, you may have heard of R, G, B — Red, Green, Blue — to express many colors. This understanding is fundamental to how we display color on monitors and how we print color.
But why
three colors
? Why not two or four or five? And how did humans discover that our eyes can "see" different colors by combining just three colors?
Today, this phenomenon is explained through the
trichromatic theory
, also known as the
Young-Helmholtz theory
, attributed to Thomas Young and Hermann von Helmholtz in the 19th century.
Less known to the development of trichromacy is another scientist —
James Clerk Maxwell's
contribution to the development of the theory.
In this piece, we explore the early experiments that led to the development of trichromacy through the less-celebrated, less-attributed James Clerk Maxwell's ingenious experiment to discover and prove the trichromatic theory.
Introducing the Apparatus
Our first step in retracing Maxwell's path is familiarize ourselves with the tool he created to conduct his experiment.
The tool consisted of a box around 6x3ft with a mirror, prisms, and lens, with a viewing hole to allow viewers to look inside the box.
Note:
The figure not to scale
As a thought experiment, imagine shining a full spectrum of white light from the viewing hole at the bottom. The white light would be dispersed through the two prisms, creating a pure spectrum to the left, revealing all the wavelengths of visible light.
Now imagine that we create slits on the left side to cover up most of the pure spectrum other than a specific section. We would only see a particular spectrum region on the other end.
Imagine that we
shine light from the other direction
. But we will only let a monochromatic light of a specific wavelength, say
620 nm (red light)
.
As the monochromatic red light enters the inside of the apparatus, only some of the rays will reach the prism. Rays that hit the inner walls of the device will be absorbed, leaving only a tiny set of rays that reach the prism and disperse at the correct angles to get to the viewing hole.
Furthermore, by the time the rays reach the prism, we can assume that they are collimated — parallel to each other — as they travel quite a distance through the tool.
When the viewer looks through the hole, they see half of it illuminated in red. This is because the prism fills only half the viewing hole with color.
The next step is where the
magic
begins.
Now, imagine what would happen if you
replaced the monochromatic light with a white light
. Similar to when we only shined red light, only a specific subset of the rays will reach the prisms. But now, the prisms will disperse the white light into a pure spectrum.
Further more, since the different wavelengths of light get refracted at different angles, from this slit position,
only light with a wavelength of around ≈620 nm will reach the viewing hole.
Even though we put in white light,
the color that the viewer sees is essentially the same
as when we only shined the monochromatic
620 nm (red light)
light in.
If we
moved the position of the slit
now, only a different set of wavelengths of light would reach the observer. The light that reaches the observer roughly corresponds to the same color of the pure spectrum formed when we shined white light from the viewing hole.
Finally, we also shine white light into the top section of the apparatus. The white light gets reflected by the mirror and creates a white color on the right side of the image that the viewer sees.
In the final setup, Maxwell had three slits created that let in light at three different positions. Since only roughly specific wavelengths reach the observer from each position, Maxwell could
create different combinations of colors by combining three distinct wavelengths
.
The width of each slit was also adjustable while keeping the center of the slit fixed. Widening and narrowing the slit width would allow Maxwell to
control the intensity
of a given color.
Although, strictly speaking, widening slit width could increase the range of wavelengths that reach the observer, in our experiment, we will assume that this setup allows us to select specific wavelengths for the viewer to see. Effectively each slit creates a roughly monochromatic light for our experiment.
By changing the position of the slits and the width of the slits, Maxwell was able to create different colors on one half of the viewing hole.
From now on, in our diagrams, we will add colors to the white light that comes in so that it is easier for us to know which color the slit positions correspond to.

data.title: A CarFax for Used PCs; Hewlett Packard wants to give old laptops new life
data.author: rubenbe
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了惠普（HP）正在开发的一个新项目，旨在为二手笔记本电脑创建类似于CarFax的系统。CarFax是一项为二手车提供历史记录的服务，而惠普希望通过类似方式为旧笔记本提供透明的历史信息，包括设备的使用情况、维修记录和性能状况。该项目由惠普的多位专家共同领导，包括Abu Baker、Sal Vasi、Barbara Spitzer和John Hong。他们的目标是通过提高二手设备的透明度和可信度，延长设备使用寿命，促进循环经济，减少电子废物。该系统还将帮助消费者和企业更好地评估和购买翻新设备。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HP在固件中嵌入遥测功能及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **支持观点**：
   - 遥测功能可以实时捕获设备健康和使用数据，提高设备管理效率，特别是在大型企业中，有助于IT经理做出更明智的设备分配和维护决策。（jamesgill）
   - 该功能可能有助于建立一个受控的二手硬件生态系统，使二手硬件交易更加安全、透明，并增加其价值。（lwn）

• **反对观点**：
   - 该功能增加了固件的复杂性，可能为秘密监控、后门和恶意软件提供机会，构成隐私入侵。（neilv, 999900000999, M95D）
   - SSD是用户在转售或捐赠电脑时唯一需要更换的部件，遥测数据存储在SSD上并不能有效防止数据泄露。（999900000999）
   - 该功能可能只是营销噱头，对实际的二手设备交易没有实质性帮助。（ok123456, trollbridge, cush, kube-system）

• **技术和市场影响**：
   - 如果HP真的关心环保，应该启动回收/翻新计划，而不是通过这种技术增加复杂性。（jamesgill）
   - 该技术可能旨在让HP控制二手硬件市场，从中获取利润，而不是让第三方翻新商获利。（lwn）
   - 该功能可能对旧设备延长使用寿命没有实际帮助，因为软件和操作系统的更新周期是旧设备被淘汰的主要原因。（OtherShrezzing）

• **隐私和安全问题**：
   - 用户担心该技术会被用于跟踪用户行为，即使更换了操作系统也无法避免。（M95D）
   - BIOS密码锁和不可替换的存储器增加了设备再利用的难度，对企业和环保都不利。（theandrewbailey, crusty）

补充讨论：
• **国际视角**：对于美国以外的用户，CarFax的类比不适用，他们不理解或不需要这种报告。（mrweasel）
• **实际效用**：用户在购买二手笔记本时，更关注当前设备的状态而非历史记录，因为笔记本的机械部件较少，维护简单。（ok123456, trollbridge）
• **企业实践**：大企业通常有固定的设备更新周期，遥测数据的精细管理对实际业务影响有限。（jamesgill）

争议焦点：
• **隐私入侵 vs. 设备管理便利**：一方认为遥测功能提供了设备管理的便利，另一方认为这是对用户隐私的严重入侵，且可能被用作不当用途。

data.title: Show HN: Open-Source International Space Station Tracker ESP32/Arduino for $20
data.author: keyth72
data.article_summary: SpaceStationTracker是一个运行在ESP32开发板（俗称"Cheap Yellow Display"或CYD，2.8英寸屏幕，价格约20美元）上的简单应用，用于显示国际空间站的当前位置。该项目使用Arduino IDE和C++开发，涉及LVGL图形库、WiFi连接、RESTful API数据获取、JSON解析以及触屏交互等技术。通过连接本地WiFi，它能实时追踪并显示空间站的经纬度和UTC时间，并提供随机空间站 facts。硬件需选用特定型号的CYD（ESP32-2432S028R），支持触屏和自动调节屏幕亮度以省电。项目代码可重新用于其他轨道物体，适合作为STEM课堂项目。编译需配置Arduino IDE，并安装相关库和文件。

International Space Station Tracker
SpaceStationTracker is an application that displays the current position of the International Space Station on a 2D world map.
It runs on a ESP32-2432S028R ILI9341 device with a 2.8" screen, commonly known as the CYD "Cheap Yellow Display",
which costs $20 or less. The code was written using Arduino IDE / ESP32 development environment in c++.
I used this project to learn programming for ESP32/Arduino/CYD.
It includes topics such as graphics using LVGL, wifi connection, getting
information from a restful API, parsing json data, and touchscreen interaction.
This would make a great space related STEM classroom project.
As of the time of writing, the end of life for the ISS is slated for 2030.
This code could be repurposed for other orbiting space objects.
Using the SpaceStationTracker
The SpaceStationTracker requires a local Wifi connection to retrieve location data
for the International Space Station. The first time you load and run the app on the CYD, it will
display a splash screen for how to connect. The ESP32 board will create a hotspot
that you can then connect to from a phone or laptop. Choose your Wifi network and
enter your credentials to connect the CYD to your Wifi. This is a safer method than
hard coding Wifi info in the application, as with many esp32 DIY projects out there.
Once the app is connected to Wifi, it will continue to display and track the
International Space Station. The esp32 will remember the last Wifi connection
when cycling power, and if it changes you will be prompted to re connect using the above method.
The splashscreen will display on the CYD until it can connect to WiFi.
On a phone or computer, connect to the temporary WiFi access point called "SpaceStationTracker".
It should show the screen above. Click "Configure WiFi".
Enter the WiFi network you wish to connect to (or select from the list) and enter your password.
This is used for the ESP32 board to connect to your local WiFi. After a successful connection,
the SpaceStationTracker app will load and begin tracking the International Space Station.
The Latitude, Longitude, and UTC date time is displayed in real time, updating from
the Where The ISS At API.
You can use the touchscreen and click on the ISS icon to display a random
fact about the ISS.
The screen brightness will dim automatically over a few minutes to save power,
and will go to full brightness again when the user interacts with the touchscreen.
Hardware Info
I bought my CYD from this link on
Amazon
for less than $20, but many places sell them.
Keep in mind there are several variations that can be called a CYD. Make sure it is the resistive touch (as opposed to

data.title: Ask HN: What's the 2025 stack for a self-hosted photo library with local AI?
data.author: jamesxv7
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：照片管理应用的功能、性能、自托管解决方案以及AI工具的整合

不同观点：
• **Immich vs. PhotoPrism**：
  - [iforgotpassword] 认为 PhotoPrism 的开发进度缓慢，特别是在面部识别和自动聚类方面存在性能问题。开发者不太接受外部贡献，导致社区贡献者流失。相比之下，Immich 开发迅速，功能强大，但界面不如 PhotoPrism。
  - 争议焦点在于开发速度与稳定性之间的权衡，以及社区贡献的开放性。

• **Ente.io 作为替代方案**：
  - [mossTechnician] 推荐 Ente.io，它具备开箱即用的面部识别和AI搜索功能，且可以自托管，满足大多数需求。
  - [nicoburns] 也提到 Ente.io 是一个具有E2E加密和自托管选项的独立商业解决方案。

• **自建解决方案**：
  - [coffeecoders] 正在开发个人使用的智能照片搜索工具，使用 SentenceTransformer、BLIP、InsightFace 等AI模型处理和索引照片，并计划进一步优化搜索性能。
  - [wooben] 分享了使用 Nextcloud 搭配 Recognize 和 Memories 应用的自托管方案，能够有效处理大量照片并具备自动上传功能。

• **其他工具和方法**：
  - [mlunar] 提到使用 CLIP 和 cosine similarity 进行语义搜索，并推荐 deepface 库用于面部识别。还介绍了 photofield 项目，专注于快速渲染和基本语义搜索。
  - [nico] 推荐使用 gemma3 结合 ollama 进行图片处理和描述生成，可以处理图片中的问题（如是否存在自行车），但处理大量图片需要较长时间。

• **重复照片和最佳照片选择**：
  - [elevaet] 强调一个有价值的功能是自动识别相似或重复照片，并选择最佳照片进行保留，以节省存储空间。
  - [gavin_gee] 希望有一个工具能够整合来自不同云服务的照片，去重并构建时间线和地理视图。

• **其他需求和设想**：
  - [ksec] 提到希望有一个类似 Apple Time Machine 的个人云解决方案，数据存储和处理在本地，同时提供云备份和软件更新订阅服务。
  - [chrisgd] 描述了一个梦想中的照片管理工具，能够自动上传、备份照片，并以小批量展示照片供用户选择和整理。
  - [ssnepenthe] 分享了一个“gallery”工具的内部文档链接，提供了高层次的系统概述，可能为构建类似系统提供灵感。
  - [weinzierl] 寻找一种AI解决方案，能够预选优质照片，类似于Apple Memories或Featured Photos的功能。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到面部识别、自动聚类、去重和AI工具的整合，反映了用户对高效照片管理和智能功能的高度需求。
- 自托管解决方案受到关注，用户希望能够自主控制数据，并根据个人需求定制功能。
- 不同工具和项目的链接提供了具体实现的参考，展示了社区中的多样化选择和实践。

data.title: Show HN: TokenDagger – A tokenizer faster than OpenAI's Tiktoken
data.author: matthewolfe
data.article_summary: TokenDagger 是一个高性能的 OpenAI TikToken 实现，专为大规模文本处理设计，提供更快的处理速度。相比原版，TokenDagger 在代码样本分词上速度提升4倍，整体吞吐量提升2倍。它使用优化的 PCRE2 正则引擎进行快速分词匹配，并简化了BPE算法以减少大词汇量对性能的影响。TokenDagger 与 TikToken 完全兼容，可作为直接替代品。安装可通过 PyPI 使用 `pip install tokendagger` 完成，并提供多种测试脚本以验证性能。项目主要使用 C++ 开发，并包含少量 Python 和 Makefile 代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++实现的AI/ML基础设施性能优化及其相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [npalli] 认为使用C++优化AI/ML基础设施中的关键性能瓶颈可以带来显著的性能提升，特别是通过在不重写整个系统的前提下替换关键部分。他还提到中国工程师在这方面表现出色。
• [chrismustcode] 赞同这种性能优化的方式，并以ScyllaDB为例，强调通过替换组件来提升性能的美学价值。
• [pama] 关注实际应用中的兼容性和便利性，建议消除vocab格式转换的要求，并提出希望看到与其他工具的双向兼容示例。
• [superlopuh] 对LLM整体性能中tokenizer优化的相对重要性提出疑问，并希望了解更多关于性能测量的信息。

补充讨论：
• [Tiberium] 建议将性能与Hugging Face的tokenizers进行比较，指出当前benchmark可能已过时。
• [p0] 提到BPE crate并询问其与当前项目的比较，特别是其支持增量retokenization的特点。
• [frabcus] 询问如何获取其他LLM的本地tokenizer，特别是对于仅提供远程API的模型，并讨论是否可以通过大量调用来推断token映射。
• [kevmo314] 分享了类似的项目经验，指出pretokenization的成本主要由regex引起，并建议考虑将regex引擎替换以优化性能。
• [fkyoureadthedoc] 建议添加WASM绑定以便在更多环境中使用。
• [pamelafox] 好奇性能改进是否能推回tiktoken本身。
• [isjustintime] 表示对性能提升的兴趣，并赞赏项目保持drop-in兼容性。
• [konsalexee] 担心简化算法可能导致tokenization质量下降，特别是忽略特殊token匹配。
• [singularity2001] 提到当前架构缺乏对某些特殊token（如NUM_FLOAT）的支持。
• [semiinfinitely] 对项目未使用Rust实现表示欣慰。
• [matrix2596] 担心tokenizer可能会对同一字符串产生不同的tokenization结果，询问是否存在标准化问题。

争议焦点：
• 性能优化的实际效果和重要性：部分评论者对C++优化在整体LLM性能中的影响存在不同看法，特别是对tokenizer优化的必要性和优先级存在疑问。
• 兼容性和质量问题：有评论者担心简化算法可能导致tokenization质量下降，以及不同tokenizer实现之间可能存在不一致性。

TokenDagger: High-Performance Implementation of OpenAI's TikToken
A fast, drop-in implementation of OpenAI's
TikToken
, designed for large-scale text processing. 2x Throughput and 4x faster on code sample tokenization.
Benchmarks
Performed on an
AMD EPYC 4584PX - 16c/32t - 4.2 GHz
.
Fast Regex Parsing
: Optimized PCRE2 regex engine for efficient token pattern matching
Drop-In Replacement
: Full compatibility with OpenAI's TikToken tokenizer
Simplified BPE
: Simplied algorithm to reduce performance impact of large special token vocabulary.
Run Tests
make clean
&&
make
pip3 install tiktoken
python3 tests/test_tokendagger_vs_tiktoken.py --tokenizer llama
python3 tests/test_tokendagger_vs_tiktoken.py --tokenizer mistral
python3 tests/performance_benchmark.py --tokenizer llama
python3 tests/performance_benchmark.py --tokenizer mistral
python3 tests/code_performance_benchmark.py --tokenizer llama
================================================================================
🎉 CONCLUSION: TokenDagger is 4.02x faster on code tokenization!

From PyPI (Recommended)
pip install tokendagger
🛠️ Dev Install
git clone git@github.com:M4THYOU/TokenDagger.git
sudo apt install libpcre2-dev
git submodule update --init --recursive
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3-dev

pip3 install tiktoken
